name: Capture a speed baseline and find the root cause

Test every template type, not only the homepage

name: Cut image weight

Self-host fonts as WOFF2 instead of calling Google Fonts

Reserve space for every element that arrives after first paint
Fix contradicting CSS rules and move late inline styles into the head

encompasses: Name the LCP element per template before fixing it
Run the fix order: un-lazy, de-animate, compress, preload, cut blocking scripts
If the image downloads fast but paints late, find the hiding script
Check TTFB before blaming the image
Preload only the LCP image with high fetch priority
Design the above-the-fold section so the biggest element is text where possible

Confirm a fix with a tap test on Add to Cart, not just the score
Track cart-completion time separately from INP
Move compatible scripts to a web worker at rebuild time

name: Build objection-handling and retargeting continuity copy

encompasses: Build one bottom-of-funnel ad per objection, not a benefit list
Add fit, sizing and returns risk to the apparel objection list
Preface a real objection early, keep the full FAQ at the bottom
Address the three blockers for a warm list: risk, price, effectiveness
Pre-empt a rival's pitch with true facts (inoculation), using a weak attack only
Reposition against a self-image or identity objection
Continue the same specific argument through every follow-up or retargeting message
Personalize a lead follow-up to exactly what they asked about, with local proof
founder_sees: The objection each bottom-funnel ad answers, sourced from real customer words.

name: Apply core direct-response copywriting rules across formats
what: Applies the account's fixed copywriting rules, reading level, sentence and paragraph pacing, single-idea discipline, proof ranking, framing defaults, to any ad, page or email line, regardless of surface.
encompasses: Run the salesman test on every line before it ships
Open every sentence with the reader, never I, we, our or the brand name
Hit a 7th-grade reading score for a thumb scrolling a phone
Cut cleverness, jokes and boasting from sales copy by default
Keep one idea per sentence and one idea per asset
Structure the body as attention, interest, desire, proof, then action
Ladder every feature to a benefit in the product's own spec units
Swap vague quality words for a concrete, checkable detail
Rank proof by strength: demonstration, third-party evidence, cost narration, analogy
Default to positive framing, use negative only when the product fully resolves it
Reserve ALL CAPS for print packaging and inserts, avoid it in digital ads
Rest the draft, then read it aloud until it stops stumbling
Cut every non-working word with a modifier sweep
Cut the lead, move the best line to the top
Run the tossed-salad audit, cutting any claim off the one idea
Score readability in code and shorten until it passes
Hold a 9-of-10 ship bar, get outside feedback first
Run the skim test: scroll without reading, check the offer still lands
Check voice consistency across a run of SKU or collection pages, 3 at a time
Preview a static in-context against real feed clutter before sign-off
Show reviewers 3 or more line versions, not just 1
Never leave a blank placeholder in client-facing copy
outputs: copy set (headline, body, CTA) in the brand's plain-language style
founder_sees: The finished copy, already checked against the house style rules.

merged_from.name: Edit and QA copy before handoff to the QA Gate
merged_from.reason: CREA-C34 (line edit and readability in code before QA) is the self-check of CREA-C26 (apply the copy rules). Same procedure.

name: Frame price and value in copy
what: Chooses how a price is framed in copy: charm versus round-number endings, cost-per-day reframes, and an honest reason stated whenever a price looks unusually low.
encompasses: Match price-ending style to positioning: charm pricing or round numbers
Reframe price as a small recurring cost per day or per use
State the honest reason when a price is unusually low
Use an apples-to-oranges comparison instead of an itemized value breakdown, when it is the fairer read
founder_sees: How a price is worded in copy, and why that framing was chosen.

name: Name products, brands and proprietary systems
what: Names a new product, method or proprietary system so the name itself carries the benefit or story, and attaches a real named person to an otherwise generic product.
encompasses: Draft name candidates that tell the benefit or story
Name a proprietary system so buyers compare methods, not commodities
Attach a real, named person to a generic product name
Test candidate names with small paid spend before committing
founder_sees: The name shortlist and the reasoning behind each one.

name: Audit the Meta ad account end to end
what: Read the whole Meta ad account (structure, naming, creative, tracking, spend) and produce one ranked 90 day roadmap naming the single biggest constraint, not a list of screenshots.
encompasses: Pull account, campaign, ad set and ad level data for the trailing 12 months from the gallery cache and a fresh Meta re-pull
Run the structure review checklist: campaign purpose lines, ad set count vs spend tier, naming, CBO vs ABO use
Run the creative review in fixed order: volume, then diversity, then quality
Score the account on a readable-data test (can results be read without guessing) and a commercial-alignment test (does spend match the business's real priorities)
Validate any proposed structure against 4 fixed questions before it goes in the roadmap
Rank findings by money at stake, not by how easy they are to fix
Write the roadmap as dated, ranked actions with the metric each one should move
inputs: connector: meta ads read (gallery cache + MCP re-pull)
founder_sees: One ranked list: here is the one thing most limiting Meta results right now, and what it would take to fix it.

name: Audit the Google Ads account end to end
what: Read the whole Google Ads account and diagnose problems top down: business, channel, campaign, metric, then root cause, following the 3 pre diagnosis rules before changing anything.
encompasses: Pull account and campaign structure, spend and conversions (manual export until a connector exists)
Diagnose any dip top down: business level, then channel share, then campaign, then metric, then root cause
Apply the 3 pre diagnosis rules before touching any setting
Find the inflection date of a change and check only the top 5 campaigns by spend around it
Match the failure mode checklist to the campaign type that dipped (Search, Shopping, PMax, Demand Gen)
Split CPA and clicks into their formula parts (impressions, CTR, CVR) to find the real cause
Default to an isolated fix over a full rebuild unless the isolated fix has already failed
inputs: connector: google ads (manual export, no read connector yet)
tools: web: Google Ads UI export (no connector yet)
founder_sees: A plain diagnosis of why Google spend is underperforming, in the order the problem actually happened, and one fix to try first.

name: Build and audit Google conversion tracking
what: Set one primary purchase action, pass real order value through enhanced conversions, and pick the tracking route (app, GTM, server side) by the brand's spend level, then check it against Shopify monthly.
encompasses: Set exactly one primary purchase conversion action, optimised to purchase, never add to cart or clicks
Never use the GA4 import as the primary purchase action
Turn on enhanced conversions and pass real order value
Pick the tracking build route by spend: app first, then GTM, then server side above about $50k a month
Add the Conversion Linker tag on all pages and turn on auto tagging
Pass product ID, category and value in dynamic remarketing tag parameters
Set conversion windows to match the purchase cycle, then check against Shopify
Track new customers with their own event, not Google's acquisition setting
Use add to cart as the primary goal only for high ticket, low volume products
Reconcile Google reported purchases against backend orders after setup and every month
inputs: brand brain: order feed, product catalogue
connector: google ads and GTM (no read connector yet, manual)
trigger: event: new account or quarterly recheck
tools: web: Google Tag Manager and Google Ads UI (no connector yet)
founder_sees: Whether Google can be trusted to report real orders and real order values, with a brief a developer can implement.
reassign_reason: Conversion tracking setup (primary action, enhanced conversions, GTM or server route) is measurement (06-MEA). This keeps it with MONEY-C20 and C21.

name: Run incrementality and lift tests
what: Design and read a Conversion Lift or geo lift test when platform ROAS and blended MER still disagree after attribution is tightened, to find the ad spend that would not have converted anyway.
encompasses: Confirm attribution has already been tightened and reconciled before proposing a lift test
Choose test type: Meta Conversion Lift, geo holdout, or matched-market geo test
Size the test: markets or audience split, minimum spend, and read window
Write the test brief: hypothesis, holdout design, read point, and what counts as proof
Read the result and update the brand's effect prior for that spend level
Never let a lift test change platform bidding directly; feed the result into budget decisions instead
trigger: event: attribution disagreement persists after reconciliation
tools: mcp: meta ads read (ads_experiment_lift_get_test, ads_experiment_list_tests, ads_experiment_check_eligibility)
founder_sees: A clear test that answers whether this spend is buying orders that would not have happened anyway, with a plain yes or no plan to run it.

name: Filter platform automated suggestions before applying them
what: Log and test every Ads Manager or Google Ads suggestion before it is applied, and separate real targeting controls from settings that are only suggestions.
encompasses: Log every platform suggested change with its stated expected effect
Test each suggestion in a small sandbox before wider rollout, where testable
Audit which targeting fields are real controls and which are non-binding suggestions
Turn off auto apply recommendations and AI generated assets by default
Record the actual effect of any suggestion that was applied, against the platform's claim
read what a given platform's agentic feature is actually permitted to change (budget, bids, creative, targeting) before granting it any permission
set a hard spend cap and a performance floor (e.g. CPA ceiling) the feature cannot cross without a fresh approval
exclude brand-sensitive categories (health claims, kids, finance-adjacent) from any autonomous creative or targeting change
pull the platform's action log after every run and diff it against the guardrails to confirm nothing was crossed
revoke the permission the moment a guardrail is breached, rather than waiting for the next scheduled review
inputs: connector: meta ads read, google ads (manual)
the platform agent's permission scope and settings
brand spend caps and performance floors
outputs: change list (apply or reject, with reason)
a run-by-run audit log with any breach flagged
founder_sees: A short list of what the platform wants to change automatically, whether it was tested, and whether it actually helped last time.

merged_from.name: Set guardrails and audit logs for platform-native agentic bidding features
merged_from.reason: Both govern platform-native automation (suggestions, Advantage+, PMax auto features) with a log and guardrails.

autonomy_reason: Turning off auto-apply and testing suggestions in a sandbox are ad-account writes. Meta is read-only, so the output is a change list for a person.

name: Design Meta account structure by spend tier
what: Pick and build the campaign structure template that matches the brand's monthly Meta spend: small, mid or large, and keep the account inside its readable data and commercial alignment tests.
encompasses: Use the small spend template: one testing campaign, optional scaling, optional small retention campaign
Use the mid spend template: 2 to 3 cold campaigns with a stated reason and higher ad volume
Use the large spend template: mandatory page strategy and bidding diversity across campaigns
Merge campaigns whose conversion volume is too thin to optimise well
Fully consolidate to one campaign only for a single product, single persona, small spend store
Split campaigns by business unit, ad sets by concept, never by launch date
Plan extra ad pages before hitting the live ad per page cap
outputs: change list for campaign consolidation or split
trigger: event: spend tier change or after audit
founder_sees: The account structure that matches current spend, as a diagram and a list of changes for someone to make.

name: Write campaign purpose lines and naming convention
what: Require a one line defendable purpose for every campaign and a fixed naming pattern for every ad set, so reporting problems get fixed with naming, not new campaigns.
encompasses: Write a one line purpose for every existing and new campaign
Fix reporting or readability problems with naming and filters before adding new campaigns
Run recurring promos in their own campaign, named for the promo
Name every ad set with persona, angle, offer, content type and launch date, never a batch name
Name ad set forks with the same concept fields plus launch date so results can be tracked across forks
define one UTM schema (source, medium, campaign, content, term) that all platforms and the affiliate network fill the same way
audit live campaigns for missing, duplicate or inconsistent UTMs
generate correct UTM strings at campaign build time instead of after launch
flag affiliate and creator links that bypass the schema and would misattribute in GA4 or the warehouse
keep a lookup table mapping platform campaign IDs to the naming convention for the daily read
catch naming drift when a human edits a campaign name inside Ads Manager or Google Ads UI
inputs: existing campaign and ad set names
GA4 or warehouse channel grouping rules
outputs: a drift report naming every non-conforming live campaign or link
tools: spreadsheet or script for UTM audit
founder_sees: One naming rule for the whole account, and which campaigns or ad sets do not follow it yet.

extensions.name: Govern UTM parameters and naming across every paid channel
extensions.what: Extend the Meta naming convention to a single UTM and naming schema shared by Meta, Google, TikTok, affiliate links and email so every paid click lands in analytics under one consistent source, medium, campaign and content field.

name: Design ad set and concept architecture
what: Define a concept as one SKU, one pain point and one offer, keep non overlapping personas apart, and load each concept ad set with enough ads for 2 to 6 exposures before purchase.
encompasses: Define a concept as SKU, pain point and offer; a change to any one starts a new ad set
Load each concept ad set with enough ads for 2 to 6 exposures before purchase, minimum 3
Launch every new concept with the concept ad plus 3 hook variations
Keep non overlapping personas out of the same ad set
Group all funnel stages for one persona in one ad set, or blend the numbers before deciding to split by stage
Spin a funnel into its own campaign once it is big enough to KPI alone
Run recurring promos in their own campaign, isolated from evergreen concepts
founder_sees: How a new idea becomes one ad set, with which personas and offers can share it and which cannot.

name: Build Meta audiences: broad, custom, lookalike, exclusions
what: Go broad in cold targeting by default, cap any interest or lookalike test as a small sandbox, and exclude existing customers from every cold campaign sized to the repurchase cycle.
encompasses: Go broad in cold targeting and let the page, price and reviews qualify the buyer
Cap any interest, lookalike or custom audience test as a small sandbox
Put the target audience in the creative and copy, not in the targeting settings
Exclude existing customers from every cold campaign, sized to the brand's repurchase cycle
Define and refresh new, engaged and existing customer segments on schedule
inputs: brand brain: customer list, repurchase cycle
trigger: event: new campaign or quarterly refresh
founder_sees: Which audiences to build or refresh, and which existing customers to keep out of cold campaigns.

name: Set placements and turn off automatic creative edits
what: Remove weak placements from store campaigns, and turn off Advantage+ creative edits and flexible or dynamic crop on every product ad so the brand's own image and copy show as made.
encompasses: Never launch placement, age or gender campaigns from breakdown ROAS alone
Remove Audience Network app rewards placement from store or engaged view campaigns
Turn off flexible or dynamic crop ads on catalogue and product ads
Turn off Advantage+ creative edits on every product ad
outputs: change list (placement exclusions, creative edit toggles)
trigger: event: after audit or new campaign
founder_sees: Which placements to drop and which auto edit settings to turn off so ads look the way the brand made them.

name: Choose Meta bid strategy and cost caps
what: Default to CBO for efficiency, switch to ABO at high AOV with low daily order volume, and win impressions with a sharper hook and clearer offer instead of raising the bid.
encompasses: Default to CBO for efficiency; switch to ABO at high AOV with low daily order volume
At large spend, run CBO with ad set minimum and maximum spend limits instead of pure CBO
Test a seasonal rotation: CBO in Q4 peak, ABO in Q1 for clean testing
Ignore cost and bid caps under about $200k a month; pick a bid strategy by business constraint
Set cost caps and bidding at ad set level, never at ad level
Win impressions with a sharper hook and clearer offer instead of raising the bid
Test whether a higher on page action rate lowers CPM before assuming a bid change is needed
trigger: event: after audit or spend tier change
founder_sees: Which bid setting fits the account's spend and AOV right now, and why raising the bid is not the first lever to pull.

name: Size Meta creative tests and read windows
what: Size every creative test with a kill rule threshold of 3x to 5x target CPA, use the budget formula (target conversions times CPA divided by test days) instead of Meta's learning phase rule, and check the test budget can actually reach that spend in the test window.
encompasses: Size every creative test with a kill rule threshold: 3x to 5x target CPA before judging
Size test budgets with the formula: target conversions times CPA divided by test days
Never derive test budgets from Meta's 50 conversions in 7 days learning rule
Match test read windows to purchase cycle and volume; never read under 5 days below $50k a month
Never judge or kill an ad on $1 to $2 of spend
Check that every ad set's planned budget can actually reach its read spend threshold in the test window
Give every test a written hypothesis before it launches
Keep one persona-and-angle pair per ad set for a clean read
Size a pack to 4 to 8 ads, plan 10 or more per concept, with a short guaranteed-delivery window
Wait at least 7 days before judging a new pack, and record a low-delivery batch as inconclusive, not failed
Exclude existing customers from cold tests
Change one variable per test, sized big enough to measure, judged by cost per purchase
Cap per-ad delivery so one ad does not starve the rest
Treat a 1-element ad, headline-only, image-only, as a test, not a default
Check LTV or category-education cost before funding a test at scale
Run a small representative test before scaling any new offer or claim
Embed a hidden verification phrase to measure real read-through
Compare total sales, not just share shift, when testing a promotion
Poll a running test against its pre-set winner, kill and read-window rules on a fixed schedule
Push one alert the moment a threshold is crossed, never wait for the next scheduled report
Test 2 to 3 thumbnail or first-frame options per video ad separately from the body-copy test
Silence repeat alerts on the same ad once the founder has acted on the first one
outputs: test brief with budget and read window
test brief (hypothesis, structure, size, read point, winner rule)
founder_sees: How much to spend and how long to wait before judging a new ad, and the exact number where it gets killed or kept.

merged_from.name: Design and structure creative and copy tests
merged_from.reason: Both set up creative test structure, winner rule and read window in the ad account. Test plans and kill rules are MEDIA's (ARCHITECTURE); CREA supplies hypotheses.

name: Apply kill, keep and scale rules to ad sets
what: Judge and move budget at the ad set level on a keep, yellow, kill table read at 3x to 5x target CPA, never touch a winning ad set directly, and find each winner's spend equilibrium by stepping budget until ROAS turns unprofitable.
encompasses: Judge and move budget at the ad set level, never on a single ad's ROAS
Apply the keep, yellow, kill decision table at 3x to 5x target CPA
Never touch a winning ad set; fork new creative into a new ad set beside it
Never run creative tests inside the scaling campaign
Do not ride one winner; clone it into variants and keep a creative pipeline running
Rescue high conviction, CBO starved ads in a small separate ad set, capped and logged
Raise winning ad set budgets in steps sized to the read window, not a fixed percentage
Find each winner's spend equilibrium by stepping budget up until ROAS turns unprofitable, then pull back
Move only confirmed equilibrium winners into a dedicated scaling campaign
Judge every budget raise over 7 or more days, never on same day revenue
Confirm a winner acquires new customers under 7 day click before briefing more of it
When doubling down on a winner, shift creative volume toward it and build the funnel around it
Flag high frequency on a top spending prospecting ad before scaling it further
founder_sees: A daily list: which ad sets to kill, which to leave alone, which to scale, and by how much.

name: Run existing customer and retargeting campaigns
what: Hold all existing customer spend in one dedicated campaign sized in dollars and frequency, ask cold spend to grow and retargeting spend to shrink where possible, and retarget non buyers with a different offer or objection, not the same ad louder.
encompasses: Ask 'where can cold spend grow' for prospecting and 'where can this shrink' for retargeting
Skip a website visitor retargeting campaign unless the engaged segment is starved of cold spend
Size existing customer ad budget in dollars and frequency, never as a percentage of spend
Hold all existing customer spend in one dedicated campaign so it cannot bleed into cold
Do not hyper segment retargeting by funnel stage, warmth tier or page viewed
Retarget non buyers with a different offer, proof or objection handling ad, not the same ad louder
Time win back or reminder ads to land just before a customer's typical reorder date
For high AOV considered purchases, run a longer nurture ladder before a same day retargeting push
Run a dedicated lapsed customer campaign with its own strategy
inputs: brand brain: repurchase cycle, customer segments
trigger: event: after audit or quarterly review
founder_sees: How much of the budget is warm traffic, whether that is too much or too little, and what to say to non buyers instead of repeating the same ad.

name: Manage dynamic product ads and the catalogue feed
what: Keep DPA out of the cold CBO in its own capped ad set, and read its results on 7 day click or incremental attribution, never on its blended platform ROAS.
encompasses: Keep DPA out of the cold CBO in its own ad set, and cap its share of total spend
Read DPA on 7 day click or incremental attribution, never on its blended platform ROAS
Check the product catalogue feed for missing images, prices or availability before scaling DPA
Check the customer and product sync into the catalogue is current
tools: mcp: meta ads read (ads_catalog_get_diagnostics, ads_catalog_get_dynamic_ads_health, ads_catalog_list_products)
founder_sees: Whether the catalogue feed is healthy enough to trust DPA, and how DPA is really performing once read correctly.
autonomy_reason: Capping the DPA ad set and moving it out of the cold CBO are ad-account changes. The output is a change list.

name: Plan the peak sale ramp and wind down
what: Ramp budget and structure ahead of a peak sale, fix a wind down date before the sale starts, and prepare the Google account for a known sale date ahead of time rather than after it opens.
encompasses: Set the ramp schedule: budget steps, new creative, and structure changes before the sale window
Fix a wind down date and budget step down before the sale starts, not during it
Prepare Google Shopping, Search and brand campaigns for the known sale date in advance
Check stock levels against the planned ramp before committing budget
Write the post sale review checklist and read point
build a dated festival calendar for the brand's category with historical demand notes where available
map WhatsApp and messaging spend uplift around Diwali, since messaging engagement runs far above other channels in that window
flag GST invoice and advance-payment timing for pre-festival stock loans as a founder-visible dependency, not a media task
size quick-commerce ad spend separately from Meta/Google for the festival window, since intent and basket size differ
set the wind-down date and post-festival RTO watch, since COD orders spike and RTO risk rises after a festival
inputs: brand brain: sale calendar, stock levels
outputs: festival ramp plan with dated budget and creative milestones
trigger: event: 3 to 4 weeks before a known sale
founder_sees: The budget and structure plan for the next sale, with a fixed date to wind it back down.

extensions.name: Plan the India festive calendar into the peak sale ramp
extensions.what: Add India-specific festival windows (Diwali, Raksha Bandhan, Holi, Eid, Onam) and quick-commerce demand spikes to the peak sale ramp plan, since these carry different messaging, stock and payment behaviour than a generic sale.

name: Set up cross border and multi market ad delivery

encompasses: Give cross border buyers their own currency, delivery time and duty messaging in ad copy
Set local payment methods, language and currency defaults for a mobile first, non US market
Show shipping cost and import duty in the Google feed for cross border orders
Run one Google feed per currency

name: Manage ad account access, ownership and multi account scaling

encompasses: Put the ad account, Merchant Center and analytics under one master login
Lock down TikTok and Meta Business access before adding any team member
Open a second ad account on the same pixel only once spend passes about $250k a month
Do not split ad accounts by country except to bill in local currency
Audit who has admin, employee or partner access on every connected account
list every admin, partner and app connected to the ad account, Page, pixel, catalog and Business Manager
flag any admin or partner with access but no active work in the last 90 days
confirm 2FA (or Meta Protect equivalent) is enforced on every admin login, not just the primary
confirm asset ownership sits with the brand and agencies hold partner access only, never ownership
produce a one-click offboarding list when an agency or freelancer relationship ends
verify the named account and customer IDs in internal records still match the live account

vendor and freelancer roster with start/end dates
outputs: access hygiene report with a stale-access and offboarding list

external_write.surface: meta ads / tiktok ads / google ads

extensions.name: Run a recurring ad account access and security hygiene review

name: Launch and structure the first TikTok campaigns

Seed TikTok lookalikes from purchasers or visitors instead of targeting them directly

merged_from.name: Design offer, bundle and price presentation

name: Design gift-with-purchase and bonus offers

encompasses: Choose gifts that help the buyer use the core product, not swag
Prefer a low-landed-cost gift over an equivalent-cost cash discount
Scale the gift with units and place it on the tier to be sold
Never gift more of the same product the customer just bought
Announce the gift at every step and require a claim action
Test any order-2 gift's payback before scaling it to every subscriber
Make bonuses practical tools or how-to content, not more reading
State bonus and kit values only at real, sellable prices
Size total bonus value to exceed the core product's price
Recover a free gift's value when the qualifying order is returned
Withhold a promised free gift on COD orders until collection is confirmed
Deliver a promised bonus unit in the second order, not the first

Set subscription take-rate targets from contribution margin
Match cadence and pack size to real use, let customers adjust it

Put a costed, reason-matched discount inside the cancel flow, not upfront
Add a founder video and clear reasons before the cancel offer

Cap pause, skip and delay; treat delay as delayed revenue, not a save

external_write.surface: subscription platform config / cancel flow build

extensions.name: EXTENSION: Add the multi-stage cancel-flow architecture and gamified non-monetary perks to the subscription offer design

Delay payment capture until a trial period ends instead of charging upfront

Proactively offer to extend a payment plan at the point cancellations cluster

name: Run the offer testing framework

encompasses: Prioritise testing offer structure before offer depth
Preselect the test metric before running an offer test
Hold creative and landing page constant when testing an offer change
Start by testing 1 offer element unless a full overhaul is the hypothesis

Re-test an offer after any change in traffic source or creative

Test a free sample or usage credit against an equal-cost cash discount

Keep testing offers even though most variants will fail

name: Set organic account and platform strategy

Pick 1 hero platform from where buyers actually spend time
Treat secondary platforms as free reach with no sales expectation
Set account type (Creator vs Business) and register from the selling country
Keep the product's visual world consistent across every platform
Adapt a proven concept's length and cut per platform, same core idea
Flag a case for funding an owned media property instead of another promotion round

name: Build the content pillar calendar and cadence plan

encompasses: Set starting cadence by catalogue shape (hero SKU vs wide catalogue)
Set a weekly posting floor the team can hold for 4 weeks straight
Rotate which SKU gets a post so no item goes untouched for a month
Confirm stock, shipping and reply capacity before a post is built to pull orders
Turn stock status into content: restocks, low-stock framing, waitlists
Post a reorder reminder for consumable or replenishable products
Track posts shipped against the floor as the only KPI in months 1 to 3
Hold the pillar mix 3 months and give the channel 12 months before a verdict
Test a scheduler against manual posting only after 4 weeks manual
Do not abandon the account after a run of weak posts
Build a rolling India festive and cultural calendar tied to the brand's category, including gifting spikes and periods to avoid tone-deaf posting
Flag festival-adjacent stock and shipping-cutoff dates so posts never promise delivery the warehouse cannot hit
Tag each calendar slot with the language variant it needs (Hindi, Hinglish, regional) so scripts are written once and localized against the same slot

idea bank (this agent's own story bank)

name: Plan founder-on-camera participation
what: Decide how much the founder appears on camera, on which account, and build fast-turnaround formats for when the founder is the only person who can film that day.

Put founder personality on the founder's own account, not the brand handle
Diagnose a sales plateau as a founder-capacity ceiling before blaming the product

Publish small posts to find the founder's voice instead of waiting to feel ready
Build a 30-minute founder-history carousel for a same-day calendar gap
Balance proof-led positioning with founder personality for considered purchases

Write comparison posts to a real, one-sentence verdict
Answer the questions buyers are embarrassed to ask
Turn shipping and returns policy clarity into pre-purchase trust content
Test warning-style vs benefit-style hooks on the same product
Run every script through a pre-publish quality checklist
Warm up with short copywork and leave an incubation gap before editing high-stakes copy
Translate and localize approved hooks, scripts and captions into Hindi and Hinglish, keeping idioms natural rather than literal

regional audience share from brand data

name: Design repeatable formats and series

Prefer formats a team can repeat many times a day without the founder

Produce a search-hit video and its companion page for a cited category term

Maintain a current list of named AI crawlers and what each one is used for (training vs. live answer retrieval)

name: Optimize product page SEO

Build the full product content stack with explicit facts, not manufacturer copy

Add first-hand experience signals to product and comparison pages

Build a dedicated page template for subscription products (cadence, pause, price-per-delivery)
Give every bundle or kit its own product page with its own keyword and spec table

Cap the FAQ at 5 questions on a product page

name: Optimize collection page SEO

Implement and validate Product, Review, FAQ and Breadcrumb schema on every money page
Deploy schema markup through Google Tag Manager when theme code access is unavailable
Keep Product, Offer and review schema accurate and validated on an ongoing basis
Cap schema investment at the level the SEO fundamentals already justify
Add Product and Offer schema to every PDP with real price and availability

Add FAQPage schema to PDP FAQ blocks built from real tickets

name: Produce content clusters and buying guides

Build and refresh seasonal category or guide pages ahead of the season, not after it starts
Map category content to the 5-stage customer-awareness ladder
Build the store's real content moat: testing notes, real customer photos, sizing data
Build a roundup or comparison page to break into a term owned by enterprise homepages

Cover a topic end to end but keep each intent on its own page type

Run a periodic content refresh review across the whole site
Refresh high-intent pages every 2 months with real new facts
Refresh a sleeper page that already has links and traffic before writing a new one

name: Run backlink, digital PR and mention outreach
what: Earn links and brand mentions through disclosed, relevant outreach: journalist queries, guest posts, broken-link and content-upgrade pitches, and review-site or listicle placements, in that priority order, never buying or swapping links.
encompasses: Never buy or swap links; disclose any sponsored placement with rel=sponsored
Point earned links at educational pages and the root domain, then pass authority inward
Screen every link prospect with a fixed checklist before any outreach
Sign up for journalist query platforms and answer relevant questions daily
Pitch guest posts and link inserts only with a real value offer, disclosed if paid
Run a backlink audit and disavow only with manual action or clear spam evidence
Prefer a link insertion, a stale-link pitch or a broken-link pitch over a new guest post
Build foundational entity links before guest posts or journalist outreach, then close the gap against competitors' backlink profile at a set monthly pace
Chase brand and product mentions before backlinks, aiming at review sites and gift guides first, then forums, then owned channels
Get onto the third-party listicles and Reddit threads AI engines already cite, participating as one named employee
Only pay for a placement the publisher itself labels sponsored or affiliate
Send a press release only for real news, and put the founder or a product expert on reporter platforms and relevant podcasts
Design a proprietary survey or data study tied to the brand's category, size the sample, and turn results into shareable graphics and a hosted page
Monitor breaking news and journalist query platforms daily for a category angle the brand can comment on within hours
Draft and get founder sign-off on reactive commentary within a 24 to 48 hour production window

reactive commentary drafts with a 24-48hr SLA

extensions.name: Run original-research PR campaigns and rapid-turnaround newsjacking
extensions.what: Beyond general outreach, run the two campaign types digital PR agencies sell separately: a data-journalism campaign built on a proprietary survey or data study, and reactive newsjacking that produces and pitches a comment or mini-study within 24 to 48 hours of a breaking story, plus standing monitoring of journalist query platforms.

name: Run local SEO and reputation program

encompasses: Run a full Google Business Profile program for any store with a physical location
Build local citations and NAP consistency
Automate posting Instagram media to Google Business Profile photos
Turn each new blog post into a Google Business Profile update
Auto-reply to positive Google reviews only; route the rest to a human
Seed a Google Business Profile Q&A with a real customer question
Ask for reviews in person right after service, not only by automated text
Ask every buyer for an honest review, never pay, script or filter it
Spread review collection across more than one platform
Keep name, price and facts identical across site, feed and every marketplace listing
Keep platform brand information current for sales-channel sync

GBP Q&A seed answers and monitoring log

extensions.name: Run named-directory citation audits and Google Business Profile Q&A seeding

name: Report and diagnose SEO performance
what: Run the fixed-cadence Search Console and GA4 read, lead with organic revenue not vanity totals, and diagnose specific problems (CTR, traffic drops, device mismatch, bounce) from the data before touching a page.
encompasses: Report organic revenue and branded vs non-branded clicks every month, never raw traffic or vanity totals
Read leading indicators before clicks in the first months of a new SEO program
Push pages at positions 4 to 30 with impressions before writing anything new
Diagnose a high-impression, low-click page by position, and retarget its title/H1 to the query that earns its clicks
Diagnose a traffic drop by finding what the losing pages share
Track organic add-to-cart, checkout and purchase by landing page
Set a fixed cadence for keyword tracking, GSC and GA4 review, device/country splits, and bounce-rate triage on content pages
Do not build a custom dashboard until a free template or export stops being enough
Run the full technical, collection-page, product-page and keyword-map audits as recurring actions
Compare device traffic against device conversion every quarter, and diagnose wrong-audience targeting with three traffic signals
Investigate a small, high-engagement referral source as a partnership, and flag first-fold CTA or template A/B tests for the Site/CRO specialist

name: Vet SEO, link and AEO vendors before hiring
what: Screen any SEO agency, freelancer, link vendor or GEO/AEO vendor pitch for red flags before the founder signs anything, and treat every vendor statistic as a snapshot, not a fact.

Track about 3 AI platforms and buy the cheapest tracker that does the job
Verify a vendor's claimed influence (for example on Reddit) before paying
Treat every AEO statistic in a vendor pitch as a snapshot, not a fact

name: Rewrite pages for answer-engine citation
what: Restructure and rewrite existing high-value pages so an AI answer engine can lift a direct, accurate answer: answer-first sections, atomic fact blocks, entity-rich sentences and buyer-phrased headlines.
encompasses: Answer every sub-question a buyer prompt fans into on one page
Open every page section with a direct answer under a question heading
Make each fact block on a page stand alone
Name the product and material; never say 'this item' or 'many users'
Write titles, H1s and openers in the shopper's own words
Build the page format that already wins the target prompt
Replace vague claims with real numbers, quotes and test data
Add one first-hand fact to every page before publishing
Write long buying guides 60% to 70% in short answer capsules
Give a proprietary material or method its own brand name
Rewrite one page end to end for AI citation, starting with the highest-traffic pages

name: Build and maintain the brand facts page and fact consistency

encompasses: Publish a brand facts page that answers every gap the prompt audit found
Make every brand fact match everywhere an engine can read it
Keep facts identical across site, schema, feed, directories and reviews

what: When an AI answer states something wrong about the brand, fix it at the source (the site) first, then the publisher it likely came from, then the wider web, in that order.
encompasses: Correct a wrong AI fact at the site first, then the publisher, then everywhere else

Ask each AI engine what it knows about the brand, then open every source it cites, and check whether the answer came from live search or memory

Treat AI-generated concepts and mockups as stimulus, not a sourcing spec

Treat saturation as demand proof only with a concrete unserved angle

Use a branded or technical-sounding name only where the claim is provable
Change exactly one variable from the category's core expectation
Borrow design and mechanics from a distant industry, not a competitor
Name a self-interested and a feel-good reason to buy for every product

Set a post-launch review date and metric before starting a test

Score every shortlisted candidate on five dimensions and rank before testing

name: Build tech packs, BOMs, packaging specs and product data records

what: Name one owner for each core store silo, write the next-hire trigger as a number (not a feeling), and run a quarterly org-chart-vs-revenue-stage review, flagging key-person risk.
encompasses: Name one owner for each of the 5 core store silos before the first hire
Write the next hire trigger as a number
Check whether the current owner of a seat is underused before hiring a second person into it
Write a hire as the missing store function, never as a generic strong hire
Put a planning/ops owner in place before the first demand surge
Name a backup for every key artefact, login and supplier relationship (key-person risk)
Run an org-chart-vs-revenue-stage review every quarter
Give marketplace and subscription channels their own named owner, separate from DTC silos
Audit for one person carrying too much of the store's decisions and build a second path
inputs: brand brain: org chart, revenue history
founder_sees: Whether the org is sized right for the current revenue, and who the store cannot afford to lose.

name: Build hiring scorecards and run structured hiring
what: Build a structured job description (silo, artefacts, metric), an honest job ad, a sourced interview question set and comp bands before a search opens, and score candidates on scorecard behaviors, not channel skill alone.
encompasses: Write a structured job description naming silo, artefacts and the seat's metric
Write the job ad honest and demanding about the real workload
Set comp bands for the role before opening the search
Use a sourced interview question set, not an invented rubric
Score a candidate on whether they will flag a bad brief out loud
Screen every hire for self-directed drive and brand-values fit, not competence alone
Look for talent past the org chart before an external search
Debate internal promotion vs external hire openly, then have the leader decide with a stated criterion
Pick sourcing channels by role (LinkedIn, niche job boards, referral) instead of one default channel for every role
Draft outreach messages to passive candidates that reference the actual role artefact
Run a structured first-screen call script against the scorecard, not an open chat
Track candidate pipeline stage and time-in-stage per role
Prepare an offer with a band-consistent number and a negotiation range before the founder calls the candidate
inputs: brand brain: role library, comp bands
founder_sees: A ready-to-run hiring pack: role, ad, interview questions and a scorecard.

extensions.name: Source, screen and support offer negotiation, not just the hiring scorecard
extensions.what: Extend structured hiring past the scorecard and job ad into the actual sourcing and screening work: choosing outreach channels, running the first screen, and preparing the offer negotiation.

name: Write onboarding and standard operating procedures
what: Write and keep current the SOPs a new hire needs in week 1 (the live operating artefacts, not just team norms), and give every operating artefact one named owner with a fixed update cadence.
encompasses: Walk every new hire through the live operating artefacts in week 1
Give every operating artefact one named owner and a fixed update cadence
Draft a new SOP when a procedure has repeated 3 times (send to founder for review before use)
Generate the account and access-provisioning checklist per role (email, Slack, Shopify admin tier, ad accounts)
Order equipment (laptop, peripherals) with enough lead time before the start date
Schedule the first-week meeting and shadow plan against the role's SOPs
Confirm every provisioning step is actually done before day one, not assumed
Flag a role that has grown past its current SOP set
inputs: brand brain: existing SOPs, artefact list
trigger: event: new hire or repeated procedure
founder_sees: A week-1 onboarding pack and one place that lists who owns every recurring document.

extensions.name: Provision accounts and equipment as part of onboarding, not just write the SOPs
extensions.what: Extend the SOP-writing job into the actual first-week checklist: what gets provisioned, in what order, and what confirms a new hire is actually ready on day one.

name: Design the weekly and quarterly management rhythm
what: Design and maintain the store's meeting cadence (annual reset, quarterly deep dive, weekly trading review, ad hoc), a visible scoreboard, and cascading messaging, sized to a small brand.
encompasses: Run 4 meeting types at a small-brand length: annual, quarterly, weekly, ad hoc
Run the weekly meeting on the jugular numbers, cancel it when there is nothing to debate
Publish every goal, owner and standard where the whole team can see it
Run cascading messaging in the last 10 minutes of every staff meeting
Set 2 meeting ground rules and defend them against pushback
Prune recurring reports and channels that have become communication sludge
Book the post-peak check-in before the peak starts
Audit a recurring meeting each quarter against known traits of an effective team
Match communication method to work type: live meetings for interdependent work, dashboards for routine work
Capture structured notes from each meeting in the cadence (weekly trading review, quarterly deep dive)
Extract action items with one owner and one date each, never a vague next step
Carry an open action item forward automatically until it is closed
Nudge an owner before an action item's date, and flag it late the day after
Roll up a visible open-items count per person for the next meeting in the cadence
outputs: Action item list with owner and date
founder_sees: A meeting calendar sized to the brand, plus the scoreboard everyone sees.

extensions.name: Turn meeting notes into a tracked action-item pipeline
extensions.what: Extend the meeting-rhythm design into the mechanics after each meeting: capturing notes, extracting action items with an owner and a date, and nudging before they go stale.

name: Run team trust, accountability and decision facilitation guides
what: Prepare structured facilitation guides (team dysfunction assessment, trust exercises, conflict and accountability tools) for the founder to run with the team, tied every quarter to one real store metric.
encompasses: Prepare the quarterly team dysfunction assessment and pair the score with one real metric
Prepare trust-building exercises (personal histories, team effectiveness, strength/weakness rounds)
Prepare conflict-facilitation guides (conflict-style read, force field analysis, role negotiation)
Prepare accountability guides (natural consequences, proposed-fix requirement, effort-based accountability)
Flag a destructive high performer or fit issue for the founder with the evidence, never act on it directly
Prepare a root-cause check for a missed launch (communication, structural, personal)
Prepare a departure communication and same-day interim-owner plan
founder_sees: A ready-to-run guide for the founder's next team session, tied to a real number.

name: Evaluate and manage vendors, 3PLs and agencies
what: Run vendor and 3PL selection by competitive RFP with a facility visit, put SLAs in writing with a stated consequence for a miss, audit every invoice against the brand's own order volume in code, and set scope, cost and review owner before any agency pod starts.
encompasses: Choose a 3PL by competitive RFP with a facility visit, never one quote
Put the 3PL SLA in writing with a pick-time clause and a stated consequence for a miss
Track delivered-on-time directly and split pick lag from carrier lag before claiming a credit
Audit every monthly 3PL invoice against the brand's own order volume in code
Re-shop freight providers monthly, compare 2-3 at a time
Set scope, cost and review owner before adding any agency pod or contractor roster
Give a 3PL the growth forecast the brand actually intends to hit, not an inflated one
Send an advance shipping notice ahead of every inbound delivery
Decide fulfilment make-vs-buy before running a 3PL RFP
outputs: invoice audit report with overcharge flags
founder_sees: A scorecard on every vendor and 3PL, and any invoice that overcharged.

name: Govern supplier purchase orders and production
what: Gate large purchase orders on a documented tech pack, run a critical path with one owner and one date per production step, and route supplier communication through one channel kept as dispute evidence.
encompasses: Never release a large PO without a tech pack on file
Pick one negotiation lever per SKU: low MOQ, low price, or short lead time
Run a critical path with one owner and one date per step; never give suppliers edit access
Build the demand forecast base excluding stockout days, using a trend or seasonal curve
Set an inventory buffer policy by volatility and capital
Keep one authoritative PO copy in accounting software and one team-visible tracker
Route all supplier communication through one channel kept as dispute evidence
Agree refund and quantity-tolerance terms before wiring a large supplier payment
Decide supplier co-development vs an independent designer before sourcing
Flag that a sourcing edge is not a permanent moat
founder_sees: Whether a purchase order is safe to release, and the schedule that keeps it on time.
reassign_reason: Gating POs on a tech pack and running the production critical path is sourcing work (PROD-C13, C16, C70). MONEY keeps the cash side (MONEY-C07).

name: Plan customer-service capacity and ticket routing
what: Staff CS tiers from the sales forecast curve, track cost per ticket, define what counts as a complex ticket before routing it, and trace a rising resolution time upstream before blaming agents.
encompasses: Staff CS tiers from the sales forecast curve, track cost per ticket monthly
Staff a pre-purchase support lane for a considered or high-AOV product
Trace a rising resolution time upstream before blaming CS agents
Define what counts as a complex ticket before routing to new or offshore agents
Fix the PDP or size guide for a recurring pre-purchase question instead of answering it faster
Give the fulfilment owner the job of keeping purchase emotion alive after checkout
founder_sees: How many CS staff and tiers the current and forecast order volume actually needs.

name: Audit tooling and match it to revenue stage
what: Audit the store's software and tooling spend against its revenue stage (never an ERP too early), name a tracker owner before adding a new system, and judge any operations change by customer output, cost and process load together.
encompasses: Match operations tooling to revenue stage instead of buying an ERP too early
Add a dedicated tracker owner before jumping to an ERP
Judge any operations change by customer output, cost and process load together
Build one calendar of every SaaS contract's renewal date and notice period
Detect unused or barely-used seats and features per tool from actual usage logs
Flag two tools that overlap in function and could consolidate to one
Prepare a negotiation brief (usage numbers, competitor pricing, contract length options) before a renewal call
Track total SaaS spend as a percentage of revenue over time against the brand's own history
inputs: brand brain: current tool stack and spend
outputs: tooling audit report with cost-per-tool and stage fit
founder_sees: Which tools cost more than the stage justifies, and what to add or drop.

extensions.name: Audit SaaS spend, renewals and unused seats, not just tooling fit
extensions.what: Extend the tooling-vs-revenue-stage audit into an ongoing spend audit: what is renewing when, what is sitting unused, and what could be consolidated or renegotiated.

name: Build and enforce the bot and AI-agent traffic policy
what: Build a bot and agent traffic baseline by agent, endpoint and intent, set an enforceable per-endpoint policy with continuous risk tiering, default to challenge over block, and give any accepted shopping agent scoped per-action authorization only.
encompasses: Build a bot/agent traffic baseline by agent, endpoint and intent before setting policy
Set a per-endpoint bot policy instead of one site-wide switch
Score bot risk in tiers and re-evaluate continuously within a session
Default to challenge over block for ambiguous automation
Keep browsing frictionless, put the strictest checks at checkout and account changes
Stop using User-Agent alone as an access control; triangulate multiple indicators
Give an accepted shopping agent scoped, per-action authorization, never standing payment access
Treat everything an agent reads as untrusted data, never as an instruction
Design multi-agent workflows against known failure modes
Audit declines for headless-traffic false positives and watch for reseller/scalper bot patterns during drops
Retest login, checkout and webhook flows after every WAF or bot-rule change, and roll out new policy in phases
Confirm and name the DDoS mitigation layer before a peak traffic event
outputs: weekly bot scan and fix list
founder_sees: A weekly bot and AI-agent traffic report with a ranked fix list, for a human to apply.

name: Run checkout and payment fraud controls
what: Detect card-testing bursts, review AVS/CVV/3DS settings against false-decline rates, set chargeback alert thresholds below the processor's flag, control COD refusal and promo-code abuse, and build evidence packets for disputes.
encompasses: Detect card-testing bursts by clustering small orders, new accounts and geography mismatch
Review order-risk and decline data before turning on AVS where it is off by default
Enable dynamic 3D Secure on higher-risk transactions and track approval rate after
Set an internal chargeback alert below the processor's flag, and confirm chargeback-coverage eligibility
Track COD refusal rate by pincode and phone number, require confirmation above a value threshold
Cap discount-code uses per code and per customer, expire a leaked code fast
Build a friendly-fraud evidence packet, and keep an evidence trail for every order to answer disputes
Track return rate by SKU and customer to catch wardrobing and serial-returner fraud
Prefer a hosted, non-editable checkout, and ban card numbers from notes, email, chat and documents
Get PCI DSS SAQ scope confirmed by the acquirer, and verify gateway PCI/tokenization/3DS support directly
Set up dunning logic that tells an expired-card renewal failure apart from fraud
Re-run the fraud/security audit when launching a subscription or new payment method
founder_sees: Card-testing and chargeback signals this week, and which settings need a human to change.

name: Harden account takeover and authentication defenses
what: Audit login, session and multi-factor authentication design: 2FA/passkeys for admins, session-cookie attributes, password hashing and rate limiting, enumeration prevention, and risk-based step-up, with recovery designed before enforcement.
encompasses: Require 2FA with passkeys on every admin account, ranking second factors and enrolling hardware/passkeys first
Decide the account recovery path before enforcing strong second factors
Remove knowledge-based security questions as authentication factors
Set Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite, Path and a bounded expiry on every session cookie, with high-entropy session IDs
Set a password policy of long and unique, breach-checked, no forced rotation
Hash any custom-login password with a maintained adaptive hasher and per-user salt
Rate-limit login, signup and reset per username and per IP
Return identical error messages and timing for wrong password vs no such user
Trigger step-up authentication on new device, new country, or many accounts from one source
Require re-authentication before changing email, password, payment method or payout details
Run quarterly phishing simulation training covering email, voice and SMS
Allow password paste and a password manager, and offer passwordless passkey login to customers
founder_sees: Which admin accounts and login flows are weak, and the exact setting to change.

name: Audit and fix web application security defects
what: Audit storefront and checkout code for XSS, injection, CSRF, clickjacking, CORS and postMessage defects, and produce a developer fix list requiring parameterised queries, output escaping, method-scoped routing and a 2-approver code review gate.
encompasses: Escape every user-rendered field by context using the framework's auto-escaping layer
Replace concatenated SQL/shell commands with parameterised queries and argument arrays
Add a stateless CSRF token and convert state-changing actions from GET to POST
Deny framing on checkout, cart, account and admin pages
Allow-list the Origin header on checkout and payment-method endpoints
Check both sides of any postMessage call before trusting the data
Replace JSONP with a CORS endpoint or server-side proxy
Add rel=noopener to every outbound target=_blank link
Serve the entire site over HTTPS, not only login and checkout
Require code review with at least 2 approvers, never edit the live theme
Stream large file downloads instead of buffering them in memory
Validate the Host header and bind to loopback on any local admin/sync tool
inputs: warehouse: site source (read, custom platform only)
founder_sees: A prioritized list of code-level security defects with the exact fix, for a developer.

name: Review admin access and least-privilege roles
what: Map every staff role to only the admin areas it needs, run a full staff access audit with same-day offboarding, monitor admin logins for new locations or devices, and issue automation credentials as revocable, scoped, logged records.
encompasses: Map every staff role to only the admin areas it needs, revoke access outside it
Restrict and alert on admin logins from new locations, devices or times
Issue every automation credential as a revocable, scoped, logged record
Run a full staff access audit with a same-day offboarding process
inputs: brand brain: staff roster and roles
founder_sees: Who has access to what in the admin, and any access that no longer matches the role.

name: Maintain backups and the incident response runbook
what: Run daily versioned backups to 3 separated locations with a ransomware-safe copy, test restores end to end, and maintain a unified incident runbook covering breach, skimming, account takeover and ransomware together.
encompasses: Run daily versioned backups to 3 separated locations, one ransomware-safe, tested for restore
Log admin, order-risk, automation-flow and DNS/header changes, with someone assigned to act
Scan storefront files for malware on a schedule; treat any detection as a breach until proven otherwise
Treat unexplained changes to shipping address, order contents or payment routes as compromise signals
Follow a fixed sequence on a skimming signal: offline, remove, rotate, check, notify
Lock or flag customer accounts and force resets after any breach touching the customer base
Build the incident runbook to handle chargebacks, fines and churn together, not as separate tracks
Run a full restore test end to end, not just confirm backups exist
founder_sees: Proof the last backup can actually be restored, and the runbook to follow if something breaks.

name: Monitor domain, DNS and brand-impersonation risk
what: Lock the domain registrar account, audit DNS for dangling records, and watch for lookalike domains, counterfeit marketplace listings and Safe Browsing blocklist flags against the brand.
encompasses: Lock the domain registrar account and audit DNS for dangling records
Watch for lookalike and IDN homograph domains impersonating the brand
Watch marketplaces and social ads for counterfeit listings using the brand's name and photos
Monitor Safe Browsing status for the storefront domain
Keep a dated record of every registered mark, domain and handle with its renewal date
Alert well before a renewal deadline, not on the day
Watch new trademark filings and domain registrations for close variants of the brand name
Watch for social handle squatting on platforms the brand has not claimed yet
Distinguish a real infringement risk from an unrelated similar name in a different category
Flag an international filing that blocks a planned expansion market (ties to BRAND-C62)
Log every flagged case with evidence for the founder or counsel to act on
Never take enforcement action; this is watch and alert only
inputs: brand brain: domain and DNS records
brand brain: registered marks, domains, handles
founder_sees: Any lookalike domain, counterfeit listing or blocklist flag found this week.

merged_from.name: Watch the brand's own trademarks, domains and social handles for lapses or squatting
merged_from.reason: Both watch lookalike domains, squatting and counterfeit listings. Keep one watch in security (23-SEC) and add BRAND-C69's trademark, domain and handle renewal dates to it.

autonomy_reason: Locking the registrar account and fixing dangling DNS records need a person with the registrar login. It is a write.

name: Audit privacy, consent and tracking compliance
what: Confirm GDPR/CCPA exposure by customer location, publish a privacy policy covering AI-agent interactions with a compliant consent banner, and remove non-payment third-party tags from checkout.
encompasses: Confirm GDPR/CCPA exposure by customer location; keep the fine and notification duty visible
Publish a privacy policy covering AI agent interactions and run a compliant consent banner
Never reuse a contact detail collected for 2FA or receipts for retargeting without separate consent
Remove non-payment third-party tags from the checkout and payment step
Re-verify current browser cookie/tracking defaults before building any measurement plan
Never repurpose HSTS as a tracking mechanism
Run a full privacy and consent check across storefront, account and checkout pages
Write the breach-notification runbook with the specific timeline each jurisdiction requires
Pre-draft the notification templates (regulator, affected customers, payment processor) so nothing is written under pressure
Maintain a repository of every signed data-processing agreement by vendor
Flag a vendor holding customer data with no DPA on file
Run a tabletop walk-through of the runbook at least once a year
founder_sees: Whether the store's privacy and consent setup matches the law where its customers are.

extensions.name: Maintain a breach-notification runbook and data-processing agreement repository
extensions.what: Extend the privacy and consent audit into the response side: a ready breach-notification runbook with the actual legal timelines, and one repository of every signed data-processing agreement.

name: Run the quarterly security audit program
what: Run the recurring four-pillar security audit with a named owner per pillar, confirm platform SOC/PCI claims before repeating them, maintain the hosted-vs-self-hosted responsibility map, and run a full threat model and vulnerability disclosure program.
encompasses: Run a quarterly four-pillar security audit with a named owner per pillar
Triage a security finding by whether a working exploit exists, not by its label
Write down which security duties the hosted platform covers vs the merchant
Confirm what a platform's SOC 1/SOC 2 audit actually covers before citing it
Verify Shopify's (or the platform's) default security claims against current documentation
Build a full store threat model weighted by peak calendar, region and past incidents
Publish a vulnerability disclosure channel with a stated response and fix SLA
Build a quarterly security review calendar covering every checklist and its owner
inputs: brand brain: platform, past incidents, peak calendar
founder_sees: The quarterly security scorecard: what was checked, what failed, and who owns the fix.

name: Mine reviews for avatar and language signals
what: Read the brand's own product reviews by star band and pull identity markers, struggle language, objections and repeated words the avatar record and copy can use.
encompasses: Pull all reviews per SKU with star rating and date
Read 1 and 2 star reviews for the real objection, not the surface complaint
Read 4 and 5 star reviews for the job the product actually did
Scan for identity markers like 'I am a' or 'as a'
Prioritize long narrative reviews over short generic ones
Discount single contradictory reviews, act only on repeated patterns
Capture every usable quote verbatim with source and date
Flag use cases no competitor targets
outputs: tagged quote set by star band
founder_sees: Kevin sees a short list of what customers actually said, sorted by how often it repeats, with the exact quotes.

name: Mine support tickets, returns and calls for struggle language
what: Read support tickets, return reasons and call transcripts as passive evidence of the customer's real struggle, separate from anything they said to make a sale.
encompasses: Pull tickets, return reasons and call transcripts for the period
Tag each by the underlying job or failure, not the surface request
Cluster repeated complaint patterns
Feed named objections into standing support macros
Flag sizing, fit or fulfilment anxieties for the avatar record
Log consent status before any quote leaves the ticket system
founder_sees: Kevin sees the real reasons people struggle or return, in their own words, not a guess.

name: Run forum and social listening research
what: Search public forums, Reddit, Quora and social platforms in the avatar's own words to find language, objections and sub-avatars a review file would miss.
encompasses: Search forums using the avatar's own words, not marketing language
Read comments on a thread, not only the original post
Use Reddit for emotional language and Quora for tactics, verified per category
Cross-check search interest terms against buying behavior
Map mass, niche and sub-avatar layers from social content
Confirm platform choice with real demographic data, not a guess
inputs: connector: social listening tool if available
founder_sees: Kevin sees what real people say about this category in public, in their own words, with the source link.

name: Mine on-site search and behavior for job clues
what: Read the brand's own on-site search terms and browse-without-buy sessions for what shoppers were actually trying to find.
encompasses: Pull on-site search query logs and no-result searches
Pull browse-without-buy session paths
Match queries to existing or missing product jobs
Flag a repeated no-result query as a possible product or content gap
founder_sees: Kevin sees what shoppers searched for and did not find.

name: Design and run customer interview programs
what: Write the interview guide, pick the channel and incentive, and run or hand off real conversations with customers to hear the job in their own words.
encompasses: Book a standing weekly slot for calls or DMs
Frame every invite as exploratory, never as sales or support
Match the incentive to the person, never cash to a high earner
Ask about the situation and struggle, never features, color or price
Cover every comparison step for a considered purchase
Log consent and storage location for every quote
Treat 1 interview as 1 data point; cluster several before changing a record
Extend interview timeline coverage for slow, considered purchases
Use a lightweight email or DM reply when a call is not possible
founder_sees: Kevin gets a ready interview guide and a place to log calls; the agent never talks to customers on his behalf without him agreeing to the plan.

name: Design and field customer surveys
what: Write short, targeted surveys, identity, post-purchase or NPS, to confirm what research found at wider scale, never to discover a new job.
encompasses: Write a short first-party identity survey for existing customers
Write a post-purchase or verification survey to confirm findings, run after interviews not before
Design a segmenting question for a pop-up in place of an instant discount
Run NPS quarterly, segmented by historical customer value
Run research separately with complaining and non-complaining customers
Cap the share of budget spent on collecting more data versus acting on it
Use an on-demand panel provider for a fast, small, directional read when there is no time for a custom-built survey
Pick panel demographics that approximate the avatar when an exact match is not offered
Treat panel results as directional and confirm anything decision-critical with the brand's own customers
Compare panel cost and turnaround against building a custom survey, and choose in code by urgency
founder_sees: Kevin gets a survey ready to send and a plain-language summary of what came back.

extensions.name: EXTENSION: Design and field customer surveys - on-demand panel option
extensions.what: Extends BRAND-C06: use an on-demand survey panel tool for a same-week directional read when speed matters more than a fully custom-built survey.

name: Research competitors and public benchmarks for avatar and positioning signals
what: Read competitor ads, pages, reviews and Q&A as public signal only, never as private data, to map the mainstream avatar, screen angles and check market health.
encompasses: Map the mainstream avatar from the Meta Ad Library
Read competitor headlines for the constraint and reward they encode
Use ad duration as a screening signal only, never proof of a winning angle
Search the Ad Library for a candidate angle before committing to it
Read competitor page polish as a market-health signal
Use a competitor demographic lookup as a cold-start seed when no avatar exists
Compare review counts across listings as a rough demand proxy
Score the brand and competitors on real category attributes
founder_sees: Kevin sees what competitors show in public, marked as signal only, never as something to copy.

name: Run AI-assisted deep research with quote verification
what: Use AI deep research as a second pass after a manual sprint, on one prioritized candidate at a time, and verify every quote at its original source before it enters a record.
encompasses: Complete one manual research sprint before running AI deep research
Run the AI report on 1 prioritized candidate at a time
Verify every quote the AI surfaces at its real source
Let AI draft the avatar record from first-party transcripts, then verify every claim
Reject any AI-drafted line that cannot be traced to a real source
founder_sees: Kevin sees a research report where every quote has been checked against its real source.

name: Draft and validate job-to-be-done statements
what: Write each avatar as a job in a situation, with the functional, emotional and social sides, validated against a verb-noun and cross-category test, never as a demographic label.
encompasses: Write the job as a situation sentence, not a need or attribute word
Record functional, emotional and social dimensions
Record push, pull, habit and anxiety forces
Name the exact thing the customer stopped using before they bought
Log the customer's current workaround as a competitor with no budget
Validate with the verb-noun test and the cross-category test
Name the dominant emotional state that sets the copy register
Re-check if the job moved before rewriting after a competitor launch
trigger: event: new avatar or quarterly recheck
founder_sees: Kevin gets one sentence that says who this is for and what situation they are in, not an age and income guess.

name: Discover, rank and prioritize avatar candidates
what: List every avatar candidate the research turned up, require a pattern across independent sources, then rank and pick the primary avatar for the current cycle.
encompasses: Run the 5 discovery lenses before settling on candidates
Require a pattern across 2+ independent sources before a candidate counts
Check niche and parent market are big enough to matter
Clear the 3 proof checks: real struggle, enough people, real want
List every candidate before deciding avatar count
Never average two candidates with different circumstance or emotion
Rank by first-party confirmation, evidence count, competition and size
Set 1 primary avatar per product line for the cycle
Keep adjacent candidates as a dated backlog instead of discarding them

name: Assemble and gate the full avatar record
what: Pull the job, forces, quotes, trigger moment and 5W profile into one complete avatar record, or mark it provisional if a required field has no evidence yet.
encompasses: Require at least 2 source types, 1 first-party, for an existing brand
Reject a draft missing a quote set, trigger moment or job statement
Assemble the 5W profile: who, what, when, where, why
Run a 60-minute research sprint and the 30-second riff test as readiness gates
Mark a first-pass sketch built only from ads and reviews as provisional
Confirm the little-hire test before crediting a win to this avatar
Check the synopsis names a real circumstance, not just age, gender, income
Draft personas by hand from the research packet's own language
Run one AI expansion round, validated against real quotes
Retire a persona once its ads stop converting
Open a new persona or use-case facet once the current one plateaus
Tag each persona with its own vocabulary and objections
outputs: persona records (belief, vocabulary, objections, plateau status)
founder_sees: Kevin sees a finished, one-page avatar record he can hand to any writer, or a clear note that it is still provisional.

merged_from.name: Build and refresh buyer personas
merged_from.reason: Buyer personas and the avatar record are the same artefact. BRAND owns avatars (02-AVT).

name: Segment avatars by tier, buyer/user, B2B and subscription

encompasses: Build a separate avatar for each price tier the brand sells across
Record 2 avatars, buyer and user, for every gift or proxy purchase
Write emotional and social fields for B2B and gift-buyer avatars too
Build a B2B ICP layer only for a wholesale or corporate line
Split the record by consequence, cohort or prior insecurity, not just condition
Build a separate churn record for subscription avatars

founder_sees: Kevin sees which customer type each price tier or gift path is actually written for.

name: Build the objection map and objection-remover pairing
what: Pair every named objection with the real thing that removed it for a real customer, and turn the pattern into support macros and a fit or size confidence angle where relevant.
encompasses: Pair every objection with a real remover, not a guess
Add a fit or size confidence angle when sizing or fit is a named anxiety
Turn named objections and failed solutions into support macros
Block any sensitive-attribute assertion about the viewer before handoff

founder_sees: Kevin sees every real objection paired with what actually answers it.

name: Maintain the verbatim language bank
what: Keep one running file per avatar of exact quoted phrases, tracked for repetition, traced to source, and anonymized, for copy and creative to reuse instead of inventing new language.
encompasses: Capture every research quote verbatim, keeping harsh wording
Track repeated words and unexpected benefit links across batches
Trace every quote to its real source and strip full reviewer names
Verify avatar phrasing is attested on the cohort's own platform
Write copy in the avatar's own recorded phrasing, not brainstormed language
Mine 5-star and 1-star reviews for exact customer phrases
Pull support ticket and chat transcripts for named objections
Run or commission 12 to 15 buyer interviews before a new product's copy
