trigger: new landing page requested, or a page-builder app named as a speed-audit root cause

name: Set up git-based theme version control and a CI deploy pipeline
what: Replaces duplicate-theme-in-admin editing with a real engineering workflow: theme code in git, Shopify CLI for local development, theme-check linting on every commit, a staging theme that auto-deploys from a branch, and a reviewed merge to the live theme, so changes are reviewable and reversible by commit instead of by remembering which duplicate is which.
encompasses: connect the theme repo to GitHub and configure Shopify's GitHub integration or CLI-based push per environment
run theme-check linting automatically on every commit and block a merge on hard errors
stand up a staging theme URL that mirrors production for every pull request
require a second reviewer or the founder gate before merging to the live theme, matching the existing AI build-agent guardrail
keep a rollback path: one command to redeploy the previous commit's theme package
tag each deploy with the change brief it shipped, so the registry can trace a live change back to its approved idea
migrate an existing admin-duplicated theme history into a single git history without losing the working live version
trigger: store setup, or after a near-miss where a live edit could not be traced or reverted

external_write.surface: store theme (staging first, production on approval)

name: Build and maintain custom app integrations and webhooks
what: Connects the store to systems no off-the-shelf app covers cleanly: an ERP, a warehouse system, a loyalty ledger, a marketplace feed or a regional courier, through the platform's API or a custom app, with auth tokens stored safely, retry logic on failed webhooks and an alert when a sync silently stops.
encompasses: map the fields that must sync both ways (inventory, order status, tracking number, loyalty points) before writing any code
build the custom app or Shopify Flow automation and register the needed webhooks
store API keys and tokens only in the platform's secure app settings or the environment's secret store, never in theme code or a public repo
add retry-with-backoff on failed webhook deliveries and a dead-letter log for ones that never succeed
alert a human when a sync gap is detected (order count mismatch, stale inventory timestamp) rather than fail silently
document the integration's data contract so a future developer does not have to reverse-engineer it
test the integration against a staging or sandbox account of the external system before pointing it at production
trigger: a manual double-entry process is found during a setup or hygiene audit

name: Run continuous automated regression testing on every theme or app change
what: Runs an AI-driven test suite before and after every theme or app change ships: visual diffs across breakpoints, scripted end-to-end flows for browse, cart, discount code and checkout, and self-healing test repair so a small DOM change does not break the whole suite. On failure it produces a video replay, network trace and a written bug report instead of a bare pass or fail.
encompasses: map the store's critical paths into test cases: home, PDP, collection filter, cart, discount code, checkout to confirmation, account login
let an AI mapping step auto-discover new or changed flows after a release instead of hand-writing every test
run visual diffs across mobile, tablet and desktop breakpoints and classify each diff as likely-noise or likely-real before a human reviews it
run the suite in parallel isolated environments so a full pass finishes in minutes, not hours
self-heal a test whose selector changed for a cosmetic reason, and flag ones that fail for a real reason
capture video replay, console errors and network trace on any failure and write a bug report a developer can act on without re-running it
gate a theme deploy on the suite passing, wired into the CI pipeline
test payment and OTP steps with sandboxed credentials, never real customer payment data
trigger: every theme or app deploy, and on a nightly schedule

name: Run real-time uptime and transaction monitoring with alert routing
what: Runs synthetic checks every few minutes against the home page, a key PDP, cart, checkout and on-site search from several regions, plus a real-user page-load feed, and routes an alert to a human the moment any of them degrades or fails, including SSL certificate expiry, instead of waiting for a scheduled housekeeping pass to notice.
encompasses: set up synthetic checks on home, PDP, collection, cart, checkout and search at a chosen interval from more than one region
add a full transaction check that walks add-to-cart through order confirmation on a schedule, not just a page-200 check
track SSL certificate expiry and DNS resolution separately from page uptime
pull real-user monitoring (RUM) page-load data to catch slow-but-not-down degradation synthetic checks miss
route the alert to the right person with an escalation path if the first alert is not acknowledged
keep an incident log with time to detect and time to fix, feeding the post-launch hygiene review
exclude expected maintenance windows from triggering false alerts
trigger: store setup completion, or after any unnoticed outage found in a hygiene review

name: Simulate AI shopper personas through the storefront before shipping a redesign
what: Runs synthetic shopper personas with different intents and devices through the storefront in a sandbox before real traffic sees a redesign, reporting add-to-cart rate, navigation path and where each persona got stuck, and compares two designs head to head so the founder sees a predicted difference before committing real ad spend to a test.
encompasses: define 3 to 6 personas matching the brand's real customer segments (first-time, repeat, price-sensitive, gift buyer)
run each persona through the current site and a candidate redesign in a private, non-indexed sandbox
record add-to-cart rate, click path length and the exact step each persona abandoned at
flag usability friction a persona hit that a human reviewer would likely also hit
compare two theme or page versions side by side on the same personas before an A/B test spends real traffic
state plainly that this is a prediction, not a measured result, and should not replace a real test on a decision with real money at stake
trigger: before a redesign goes to a real A/B test, when the change is expensive to build

name: Reduce COD return-to-origin (RTO) with checkout-side automation
what: Builds the site-side half of India's COD RTO problem: a PIN code serviceability check on the PDP before the shopper commits, address auto-fill with OTP verification on high-value COD orders, a visible small COD fee to filter impulse orders, a prepaid discount incentive shown at checkout, a WhatsApp order-confirmation trigger with an auto-cancel rule on no reply, and a branded tracking page, each measured against the brand's own RTO rate by PIN code and payment method.
encompasses: show real-time PIN code serviceability on the PDP using the courier or aggregator's API before the shopper adds to cart
add address auto-fill and phone OTP verification at checkout for COD orders above a set value
add a visible COD handling fee as a checkout line item, sized to filter impulse orders without losing genuine buyers
surface a prepaid discount or free-shipping incentive at the exact checkout step where COD is selected
trigger an automated WhatsApp order-confirmation message after COD checkout, with an auto-cancel rule if unconfirmed within a set window
replace the generic courier tracking link with a branded tracking page that also carries post-purchase upsell content
pass a buyer risk score (first order, high COD value, prior RTO history) to the fulfilment system so it can flag for manual check, without the site itself running the logistics side of NDR handling
build an RTO analytics view by courier, PIN code, product and payment method so the founder can see which lever is moving the number
Identify pincodes and customer segments with COD share and RTO rate above brand average
Design the test: prepaid-only, partial advance, or a COD convenience fee, on a defined slice of traffic
Set the read point: conversion-rate change against RTO-rate change, not conversion alone
Blacklist or flag a serial-RTO customer for COD ineligibility on future orders
inputs: order data by pincode and customer
trigger: COD share and RTO rate identified as a bottleneck in the metric contract

external_write.surface: store checkout settings, WhatsApp business account

merged_from.name: Run a COD-to-prepaid conversion test program
merged_from.reason: Both change checkout payment options for COD-heavy pincodes (prepaid-only, partial advance, COD fee). The surface is checkout (SITE).

name: Track platform release notes and plan feature adoption or migration
what: Reads each platform release (Shopify Editions twice a year, WooCommerce and WordPress core updates, an installed app's deprecation notice, an API version sunset date) and turns it into two short lists for the founder: native features that can now retire a paid app, and breaking changes that need a fix before the sunset date, so the store never gets caught by a deprecation it did not see coming.
encompasses: read each Shopify Editions release and the platform's API version deprecation calendar on its schedule
match new native features against the brand's current paid app list to flag a possible app to retire
flag any announced breaking change against code the store actually uses, not a generic checklist
set a reminder ahead of every API version sunset date the store depends on
write a short adopt-or-ignore recommendation per release, not a full changelog dump
check WooCommerce or custom-platform framework updates the same way when that is the brand's platform
inputs: current app and API version list
trigger: a platform release lands, or a deprecation notice arrives

name: Maintain a site-wide design system and component library
what: Documents the brand's spacing, color, typography and button tokens once, then checks every new theme section and page-builder page against them, so a landing page built in a page-builder app does not drift from the native theme's look, and hands a developer or builder a spec instead of a screenshot to match by eye.
encompasses: document color, spacing, typography and component tokens from the current live theme
check every new homepage or PDP section, whether built natively or in a page-builder app, against the token set before it ships
flag drift: a button radius, font size or color that does not match the documented token
produce a Figma-to-Liquid or Figma-to-builder handoff spec for a new section so a developer does not guess spacing from a picture
keep one canonical component list so the same 'FAQ block' or 'comparison table' is not rebuilt slightly differently five times
trigger: a new page or section is briefed, or a drift is spotted in QA

name: Maintain a staging environment that mirrors production data and theme
what: Keeps a staging copy of the store, theme and a recent product and price snapshot in sync with production, so a change, an app trial or a migration can be tested against real-looking data before it ever reaches a live customer, separate from the CI pipeline's code-only staging theme.
encompasses: stand up a staging store or sandboxed duplicate on the same platform
refresh its product, price and inventory snapshot from production on a schedule, never the reverse
mirror the live theme and installed app list into staging before a risky change
password-protect the staging store and keep it out of search indexes
tear down or reset staging data on request so it never becomes a second source of truth
use staging, not production, for every app trial and every AI build-agent session
trigger: store setup, or before any change flagged as risky

name: Build no-code automation rules for site-side operational triggers
what: Uses the platform's own automation layer (Shopify Flow or equivalent) to wire small operational rules directly into the store instead of a developer hand-coding each one: auto-tag a high-risk COD order, auto-hold an order from a flagged RTO offender, auto-apply gift wrap above a cart value, auto-alert the founder on a stockout of a top SKU on its own PDP.
encompasses: list the recurring manual actions a store manager currently does by hand that are pure if-this-then-that logic
build each rule in the platform's native automation tool so it needs no custom app and no hosting
test each rule against a real historical order before turning it on live
log every automated action it takes so a human can audit what fired and why
avoid stacking automation rules that touch the same object in a conflicting order
route anything that needs judgment, not just if-then logic, to a human queue instead of automating it
trigger: a repetitive manual task is found in a hygiene or ops audit

name: Set up a self-serve returns and exchange portal on-site
what: Configures a customer-facing returns and exchange flow on the store (a dedicated app or a native flow), with exchange-for-store-credit incentives sized against real margin, so a return does not always mean a lost sale, and hands the fulfilment-side restocking rule to ops rather than building it itself.
encompasses: select and configure a returns app or native flow against the brand's actual return window and condition rules
set an exchange-for-store-credit incentive with a real bonus amount the margin can support
surface return reasons in a structured way so the data feeds product and copy fixes elsewhere
keep the return portal's copy consistent with the published returns policy page word for word
hand the restocking and refund-timing rule to the operations specialist instead of building warehouse logic here
test the full return-request-to-resolution flow as a real customer would
trigger: a high return or exchange volume is found in hygiene monitoring

name: Support agentic checkout for third-party AI shopping assistants
what: Makes the store's product data, pricing and checkout machine-readable enough for a third-party AI shopping assistant acting on a shopper's behalf to find a product and complete a purchase, then tests that path end to end, since this channel is new and unproven but growing.
encompasses: verify the product feed and structured data an outside AI agent would read (price, stock, variant, shipping cost) are accurate and current
check the checkout can complete a purchase from an agent-initiated session without a broken step a human would silently work around
confirm order attribution correctly tags an agent-initiated purchase so it does not get miscounted as organic or paid
flag any step (a CAPTCHA, a mandatory account creation) that blocks an agent from completing a purchase, and decide with the founder whether to relax it
keep this channel read-only in measurement until the founder has seen at least a handful of real agent-driven orders
trigger: agent-driven orders start appearing in order source data, or the founder asks about this channel

name: Auto-sequence PDP images from the brand's own click-map and zoom data
what: A capability no tool sells yet: instead of a human guessing a better product-image order and running a slow A/B test, the agent reads which images shoppers actually zoom into, skip past or abandon on, and proposes a re-sequenced gallery ranked by real attention data, with the reasoning shown so the founder can approve before it ships.
encompasses: pull per-image zoom, dwell and skip events from the site's own click-map or session-replay data, never a generic benchmark
rank the existing image set by which ones hold attention longest before a scroll-away or an add-to-cart
propose a re-sequenced gallery order with the reasoning per swap, not just a new order with no explanation
flag when there is not yet enough session volume on a SKU to trust the ranking, and say so instead of guessing
size this as a proposal for the founder gate, not an automatic live change, since it touches a live PDP
inputs: click-map or session-replay data per PDP
trigger: a PDP has enough session volume and an unresolved add-to-cart drop-off

name: Cap exit-intent and cart-abandonment discounts to a margin-safe ceiling in real time
what: A capability no tool sells yet: an exit-intent popup or an abandoned-cart discount is normally a single flat number set once by a human. Here the agent computes, in code, the maximum discount that specific cart can take and still clear the brand's real per-order margin floor, using landed cost and shipping cost already in the brand record, so the offer flexes by cart instead of guessing one number for every visitor.
encompasses: read landed cost, shipping cost and any active promo already applied for the exact cart at the moment of exit intent
compute the maximum discount in code that still clears the founder's set margin floor for that order
never let the model estimate the number; the ceiling is arithmetic from the brand's own cost data
show the founder the ceiling logic before turning the offer live, and cap it below the computed ceiling if the founder wants a buffer
fall back to no discount, not a guessed discount, when a cost input for that SKU is missing
trigger: exit-intent or cart-abandonment offer is being designed or already underperforming

name: Build an on-site visual product search from an uploaded photo
what: A capability no tool sells yet at the brand's scale: a shopper uploads or snaps a photo (a style they saw elsewhere, or a product they already own) and the site returns the closest real SKUs by visual similarity, using an image embedding model matched against the brand's own product photos, kept separate from any competitor-image use since only the shopper's own photo is compared, never stored as a competitor asset.
encompasses: embed every live product's real photos once and keep the index current as the catalogue changes
accept a shopper-uploaded photo, embed it the same way, and return the nearest real SKUs, never a generated or redrawn product
cap the feature to product discovery only; never claim a visual match is exact
fall back cleanly to text search when no close visual match exists
keep uploaded shopper photos private and short-lived, never stored as training or competitor data
trigger: on-site search bottleneck diagnosed and the catalogue is visually distinct enough to benefit

name: Add a click-to-WhatsApp catalog and buy flow on the PDP
what: Adds a pre-purchase WhatsApp channel for India: a click-to-WhatsApp button on the PDP that opens a chat pre-filled with the exact SKU and variant, backed by the brand's WhatsApp catalog, for shoppers who trust a chat conversation with a human or a bot more than a cart, and routes the resulting cart-recovery and support load to the lifecycle specialist rather than handling it here.
encompasses: sync the live product catalogue (price, stock, variant) to the brand's WhatsApp Business catalog on a schedule
add a click-to-WhatsApp button on the PDP that pre-fills the exact SKU, variant and a template question
confirm the button only appears where WhatsApp commerce is legal and commonly used, not on every market
measure how many PDP-to-WhatsApp clicks convert to an order, separate from normal add-to-cart, so it is not double-counted
hand the WhatsApp conversation flow itself, cart recovery and support scripting to the lifecycle specialist
trigger: India market with COD or trust-driven checkout hesitation diagnosed as a bottleneck

external_write.surface: store PDP template, WhatsApp Business catalog

name: Configure consent-based tag gating for India's DPDP Act and GDPR
what: Builds a cookie and tag consent layer that actually gates tracking scripts by the visitor's region and choice, rather than a banner that shows for legal cover while every pixel fires anyway, covering both India's DPDP Act for Indian visitors and GDPR for EU visitors on the same store.
encompasses: inventory every tracking pixel, tag and script currently firing on first page load
route each one behind a consent-management layer keyed to visitor region and explicit choice
confirm a rejected-consent visitor genuinely does not fire the gated scripts, by checking network requests, not just the banner's own claim
set the correct default (opt-in for GDPR regions, per DPDP's stricter consent requirements for India) rather than one global default
keep essential, non-tracking scripts (cart, checkout, payment) ungated so consent choices never break core function
log consent choices in a way the brand can produce as proof if ever asked
trigger: store setup for an India or EU-facing brand, or a compliance audit finding

name: Build a restock waitlist and pre-launch password-page capture flow
what: Adds a notify-me capture on an out-of-stock PDP and a password-protected coming-soon page for a pre-launch or a limited drop, each wired to collect an email or WhatsApp number and fire an automatic notification the moment stock or launch goes live, instead of losing that demand silently.
encompasses: add a notify-me form on any out-of-stock PDP, capturing email or a WhatsApp number where that channel is in use
fire an automatic notification the moment the SKU is back in stock, ranked by signup order for a limited restock
build a password-protected coming-soon page for pre-launch or a drop, keeping it out of search indexes
capture waitlist signups into the brand's own list, never a third party's, so it feeds lifecycle directly
report waitlist size and back-in-stock conversion rate per SKU to size real demand before a reorder decision
trigger: a top SKU goes out of stock, or a pre-launch or drop is planned

name: Watch competitor pricing and refresh truthful anchor-price copy on the PDP
what: A capability no tool sells yet in this exact form: reads the same publicly listed competitor prices used for reference elsewhere in the system on a schedule, and when the brand's own PDP carries an anchor-price comparison claim, checks it is still true and flags it for a copy refresh the moment a competitor's public price moves, so a comparison claim never goes stale or false, without ever copying competitor text, images or branding onto the page.
encompasses: read only publicly listed competitor prices already treated as signal elsewhere in the system, never scraped account data
match each PDP anchor-price or comparison claim to the specific competitor price it cites
flag a claim as stale the moment the cited competitor price changes enough to make the comparison inaccurate
propose the corrected comparison number for a human to approve before the copy changes
never let a comparison claim ship without a current, dated source behind it
keep this entirely separate from the brand's own private cost and margin data
trigger: a competitor price change is detected, or a scheduled weekly check

name: Prepare bulk ad-launch upload sheets
what: Turns an approved batch of ad copy and creative filenames into the exact spreadsheet or CSV a bulk-upload tool or Ads Manager's own bulk editor expects, one row per ad, so a person only reviews and clicks launch.
encompasses: Map each creative file, headline, primary text and CTA to the platform's required CSV columns
Apply the account's fixed naming convention to every campaign, ad set and ad name in the sheet
Carry over only the budget, audience and placement values the media buyer already approved, never invent one
Flag any row missing a required field before the sheet is handed over
Produce a separate sheet per platform since Meta's bulk editor and TikTok's bulk tool use different columns
Version each sheet so a re-upload after edits does not create duplicate ads
inputs: media buyer's approved budget and audience plan
trigger: event: creative batch approved for launch
founder_sees: The exact sheet that will go into Ads Manager, ready to check before anyone clicks launch.

name: Generate synthetic AI-actor UGC video ads end to end
what: Turns a written script into a finished vertical video ad using a licensed AI actor who reads the hook to camera, without booking a human creator or a shoot, for early testing before real UGC is commissioned.
encompasses: Pick an AI actor whose look and delivery match the brief's persona, not a random default
Feed the actor the exact approved script line by line, never let the tool improvise a claim
Generate 3 to 5 hook variants of the same script for a cheap pre-test before commissioning a real creator
Add on-screen captions and a CTA card in the brand's own template
Run every generated line through the claim and compliance check before it is used
Label every synthetic-actor ad as such in the internal tagging system, never pass it off as real UGC to the founder
Reserve real human UGC for anything a synthetic actor cannot say honestly, such as a real before-after story
outputs: finished vertical video ad, several hook variants
founder_sees: The generated video, clearly marked as an AI actor, before it enters testing.
autonomy_reason: Spends on licensed AI-actor generation. A synthetic person reading a hook to camera can read as an invented testimonial, which touches the no-invented-people red line.

name: Generate ad variants directly from a product page URL
what: Reads a live product page, pulls its images, price and stated claims, and drafts a first-pass set of static and video ad variants from it, as a fast starting point the strategist edits rather than a blank page.
encompasses: Pull product images, price, variants and stated specs from the page, never invent a spec not on the page
Draft 3 to 6 ad concepts (different hooks, same product facts) from the page content
Flag any page claim that is not already tiered in the brand record, for the compliance check to resolve
Match the drafted CTA to the page's actual buy button and current offer, not a stale one
Re-draft automatically if the source page's price or stock status changes before launch
outputs: first-pass ad concept set (static and video)
source-page fact list with URL and date
founder_sees: A first draft built straight from the live product page, ready to edit.

name: Manage creator whitelisting and Partnership/Spark Ads authorization
what: Runs the technical steps that turn a creator's organic post into a paid whitelisted or Spark ad, checks the prerequisites first, and tracks every authorization code and its expiry.
encompasses: Check the creator's Instagram is linked to a Facebook Page before requesting Partnership Ads access, the most common blocker
Walk the creator through generating the 8-digit TikTok Spark Ads code or Meta Partnership Ads authorization
Log each code with the post it belongs to, the date issued and the date it expires
Confirm the authorized post matches the exact creative and copy the brief approved, not a different cut
Flag a code nearing expiry so the ad can be relaunched before it drops
Keep whitelisting requests to pages that already post well organically, never a dead account
inputs: creator brief and usage rights log
trigger: event: creator content approved for paid use

external_write.surface: Meta Partnership Ads authorization; TikTok Spark Ads code exchange

founder_sees: Which creators are ready to whitelist, which are blocked and why, and when each code expires.
reassign_reason: Partnership Ads and Spark authorisation is ad-account setup, like MEDIA-C26's Spark codes. CREA owns the asset, not the ad account.

name: Auto-resize and reformat one master creative into every placement spec
what: Takes one approved master creative and produces every aspect-ratio and placement version a platform needs, feed square, story vertical, in-stream widescreen, recomposing the focal point rather than stretching or cropping blind.
encompasses: Recompose the safe zone and focal point per aspect ratio, never a blind crop that cuts off the product or CTA
Produce the fixed set: 1x1, 4x5, 9x16 and 16x9 from one master file
Re-time text and caption cards to fit the shorter frame of a 9x16 cut
Check every resized version keeps the CTA and price fully visible, not clipped by platform UI overlays
Flag a master creative whose composition cannot be safely resized, so it gets reshot for that placement instead of stretched
outputs: full placement set of resized creative
founder_sees: One approved creative, already delivered in every size a platform will ask for.

name: Generate captions, burned-in subtitles and alt text for every ad asset
what: Adds accurate burned-in captions to every video ad, since most are watched muted, and writes descriptive alt text for every static image, as a fixed QA step before anything ships.
encompasses: Transcribe the finished voiceover or on-screen speech and burn in captions matched to the brand's caption style
Time captions to the cut, never let a line run past its shot
Write alt text for every static and carousel image describing the product and offer, not just the file name
Check caption wording against the claim rules since a caption is still a claim
Support at least one non-English caption set where the localisation spec calls for it
founder_sees: Nothing directly. This is a fixed QA step before an ad ships.

name: Auto-cut one master video ad into multiple length and aspect-ratio derivatives
what: Cuts one finished long-form video ad into a family of shorter derivatives, a 15-second and a 6-second bumper cut, each keyed to a different hook from the hook bank, without a fresh edit session per cut.
encompasses: Cut to the strongest hook variant already tested in the hook bank, not an arbitrary trim
Keep the proof and CTA beat in every derivative even at 6 seconds
Produce a story-style vertical cutdown and a feed-style square cutdown from the same source
Re-time captions to each new cut length
Tag each derivative back to its parent video and the hook it uses, for the winner teardown to trace later
outputs: set of length and aspect-ratio derivatives, each tagged to its parent
founder_sees: The same winning video, already cut into the short lengths a platform actually rewards.

name: Score new creative for predicted performance before spend
what: Runs a draft creative through a predictive scoring pass before it enters a paid test, flagging weak elements (hook clarity, headline-image mismatch, CTA visibility) so a likely loser is fixed or dropped before it spends real budget.
encompasses: Score a draft's visual and copy elements against patterns from the account's own past winners and losers, not a generic industry model alone
Flag a specific weak element (hook, image-text mismatch, buried CTA), never just a single opaque score
Rank a batch of drafts so the weakest gets fixed or cut before it enters the test budget
Treat the score as a filter before spend, never as the final word after real results exist
outputs: pre-launch score per draft, with flagged weak elements
trigger: event: before a new batch enters paid testing
founder_sees: Which drafts in this batch are likely weak, and why, before any of them spend money.

name: Generate catalogue-scale ad variant grids from the product feed
what: Combines a fixed template, the product feed's price and image fields, and a small set of copy blocks to produce a full grid of ad variants across hundreds of SKUs at once, instead of building each SKU's ad by hand.
encompasses: Read price, image, title and stock fields straight from the product feed, never a stale copy
Apply a fixed set of template x headline x CTA combinations across every SKU in the grid
Skip a SKU with a missing image or price rather than publish a broken variant
Cap grid size to what the account's own testing budget can actually read
Regenerate only the SKUs whose feed data changed, not the whole grid, on a refresh
trigger: event: new catalogue campaign, or on feed refresh
founder_sees: How many SKUs got a ready ad variant this run, and which ones were skipped and why.

name: Write and design COD-to-prepaid conversion and RTO-reduction creative messaging
what: Writes the ad and post-purchase creative lines that push a cash-on-delivery order toward prepaid, and the delivery-trust messaging that lowers return-to-origin risk, since both are India-specific costs a generic ad script ignores.
encompasses: Write the prepaid-incentive line (small discount or free shipping) framed as unlocking a benefit, never as a penalty for choosing COD
Write the WhatsApp or SMS follow-up message offering the same incentive with a payment link inside a short window after a COD order
Write delivery-trust lines (real dispatch time, real carrier, easy return) that reduce the buyer's reason to reject at the door
Check every prepaid or RTO claim (discount amount, delivery time) against the brand record before it ships
inputs: brand brain: shipping and payment policies
founder_sees: The exact lines that will nudge a COD order to prepaid, and the numbers behind them checked against your policy.

name: Build Amazon A+ Content and Flipkart/Myntra brand-store creative modules
what: Designs the banner, infographic and comparison-chart modules for a marketplace's own A+ Content or brand-store template grid, since these follow a fixed module system unlike a normal ad canvas.
encompasses: Design each module (hero banner, feature comparison, lifestyle image, spec table) to the marketplace's exact pixel and module-count limits
Reuse the brand's approved claims and real product photos, never a new unchecked claim written just for this module
Build a separate module set per marketplace (Amazon A+, Flipkart brand store, Myntra brand page) since their templates differ
Flag a module that would look identical to the standard listing images, since A+ content should add new information, not repeat it
inputs: marketplace's current template grid and size limits
outputs: A+ Content or brand-store module set, per marketplace
founder_sees: The finished module set, ready to upload to the marketplace's own content manager.

name: Clone a consenting voice for scaled ad voiceover variants
what: Clones the founder's or a contracted creator's own voice, with their documented written consent, to produce many voiceover script variants without booking a new recording session for every script change.
encompasses: Require documented written consent naming voice cloning, commercial use and every channel the audio will run on, before any clone is made
Generate the voiceover for each approved script variant from the cloned voice, never let the voice model improvise a line
Re-generate a voiceover in minutes when a script edit changes only a few words, instead of a new studio session
Retire and delete a cloned voice the moment the person's consent window ends
inputs: consenting person's voice sample and signed consent
trigger: on demand, only after consent is on file
founder_sees: The consent on file and the generated voiceover, before any script variant using it goes further.

name: Build and maintain a consistent AI character or mascot sheet for reuse
what: Builds a fixed reference sheet for a generated character or mascot, expressions, angles, outfit, so every later AI-generated image or video reuses the same identity instead of a new random face each time.
encompasses: Generate a character sheet: front, side and three-quarter views, a few expressions, in the brand's chosen style
Reference the same sheet on every later generation so the character does not visibly drift between assets
Version the sheet if the brand deliberately updates the character's look, and retire the old version everywhere at once

name: Compute true customer profitability and feed it into segmentation and loyalty tiering
what: Adds support-ticket cost, return/refund cost, shipping cost and discount cost against each customer's revenue, in code, so VIP and loyalty tiering rewards the customers who are actually profitable rather than the ones who simply spend the most and cost the most to serve. No loyalty platform ties reward cost to measured cost-to-serve this directly today.
encompasses: Estimate a per-ticket support cost and attach it to the customers who filed tickets
Attach return/refund cost (product, shipping both ways, restocking) to the customer who returned
Attach discount cost actually redeemed, not list price, to each customer
Compute a profitability figure per customer, all arithmetic in code, never modelled by the model itself
Compare the profitability ranking against the revenue-only RFM ranking and flag the customers that move a lot
Feed the profitability figure into loyalty tier and VIP-treatment decisions as a second input, not a replacement for revenue
Show the founder both rankings side by side before any tiering change, since this reshuffles who counts as a VIP
inputs: support ticket volume and estimated cost
outputs: a comparison against the revenue-only ranking
trigger: quarterly, or before a loyalty tier redesign
founder_sees: both rankings side by side and the customers that move
reassign_reason: True customer profitability (support, returns, shipping and discount cost per customer) is a margin model. MONEY computes it; LIFE uses it for tiers.

name: Handle data-subject access and erasure requests under India's DPDP Act

Field it by email, WhatsApp or a short call within days of the decision, while memory is fresh
Separate the stated reason from the real deciding factor
Tag every response to a specific competitor and a specific decision factor (price, trust, delivery, review)
Roll results into the objection map (BRAND-C13) and the category ladder (BRAND-C18) evidence base
Flag a competitor advantage that recurs, since it is a product or policy problem, not a copy problem
Keep sample size small and repeat quarterly rather than one large one-time study
outputs: win-loss findings by competitor and factor, with quotes
tools: connector: whatsapp business (read-only for existing threads)

name: Diagnose the gap between intended and actual brand perception
what: Compare what the brand says it stands for (positioning statement, voice sheet, claims) against what customers actually say in reviews, social mentions and survey results, and name the gap.
encompasses: Pull the current positioning statement, voice sheet and top claims from the brand brain
Pull the most repeated words and sentiments from reviews and social listening
Score each intended attribute as confirmed, contested, or absent in the real signal
Name the single biggest gap, not a list of ten
Distinguish a messaging problem (right positioning, wrong words) from a product problem (wrong positioning)
Check whether the gap is new or has persisted across the last audits
Recommend whether the fix is a messaging change, a proof change, or a repositioning trigger
Feed a confirmed repositioning-level gap into the rebrand process (BRAND-C49)
inputs: brand brain: positioning, voice sheet, claims
outputs: perception gap report with evidence per attribute
trigger: quarterly, alongside the brand consistency audit (BRAND-C37)

Search for publications running bylined or guest columns in the category
Match each opportunity to a specific angle from the founder's story or a real result
Draft a short, specific pitch email per opportunity, never a generic one
Track which opportunities are live requests (a journalist looking for a source now) versus evergreen
Log outcomes: accepted, declined, no reply, to avoid re-pitching a dead lead
Prepare a one-page founder briefing (talking points, no invented numbers) before any accepted slot
Never commit the founder's time without approval

trigger: monthly sweep, plus on demand around a launch

Match the brand's own proof (real numbers, real reviews) to each award's criteria

Track submission deadlines and required assets (photos, samples, executive bio)
Log outcomes and turn a real win into an approved, site-backed claim
Flag when a submission fee is required so the founder can decide
Keep a dated log so the same award is not missed or duplicated next cycle

name: Run a new-market entry feasibility assessment

Check labeling and packaging rules that differ from the home market
Map the competitor set already serving that market at the brand's price point
Check shipping, customs and return logistics options and their real cost
Check payment method norms (COD prevalence, card penetration, local wallets)
Estimate a landed cost and price point for the target market from the brand's own cost data
Flag any legal restriction on the product category in that market
Score the market as go, go-with-conditions, or not-yet, with the specific blocker named
inputs: brand brain: product costs and specs
outputs: market feasibility report per candidate country
trigger: on demand, when a new-market wild bet is proposed
founder_sees: Kevin sees whether a new country is actually legally and logistically workable before any market-sizing conversation happens.
today_done_by: nobody at this size, or a consultancy

name: Model and structure a brand licensing deal
what: For a proposed licensing opportunity, check royalty norms, build a licensee scorecard and draft the deal memo terms for the founder to negotiate from.
encompasses: Check the typical royalty rate range for the product category and exclusivity level
Score a candidate licensee on production capability, distribution reach and brand fit
Draft the deal memo: royalty rate, minimum guarantee, term length, territory, approval rights
Require an approval step for product, packaging and promotional material in every draft
Flag category overlap with an existing wild bet or product line
Model the brand's expected royalty income against the licensee's own sales estimate
Check the licensee's public reputation for quality or legal issues
Keep every draft a proposal only; no term is final until the founder signs

Compute the wholesale margin the retailer keeps at a typical retail markup
Draft the buyer pitch deck: brand story, proof (sell-through, reviews, press), assortment plan
List the retail terms options: net terms, consignment, minimum order value
Flag which SKUs are protected by an existing exclusivity or DTC-only policy
Check packaging and labeling meet retail shelf requirements, not just DTC unboxing
Prepare a one-page leave-behind for a trade show or buyer meeting
Keep pricing consistent with the brand's own pricing position audit (BRAND-C24)

founder_sees: Kevin gets a real line sheet and buyer deck ready for a trade show or a retail meeting, instead of building one from scratch under deadline.
human_role: expansion or new markets lead, brand manager
today_done_by: nobody at this size, or a freelancer

name: Run AI-persona pretesting of messaging, names and concepts
what: Before spending on a real survey or interview round, run a quick AI-simulated persona pass on a messaging, naming or concept shortlist to catch obvious misses early, always labeled directional.
encompasses: Build the persona from the brand's own validated avatar record, not a generic demographic guess
Run the shortlist (names, headlines, concepts) past the simulated persona for a reaction
Ask the same follow-up questions a real interview would ask, to surface reasoning, not just a verdict
Flag any response that just repeats the input back, a sign the simulation adds no information
Never treat a synthetic result as validated; label it clearly as a pre-filter
Use it only to cut an oversized shortlist before spending on real research (BRAND-C05, BRAND-C06)
Log where the synthetic read and the later real result agreed or disagreed, to calibrate trust over time
Stop using it for a given decision type if it disagrees with real results more than it agrees
outputs: synthetic reaction summary per shortlist item
trigger: on demand, before a real research round

Complete a real checkout and note every friction point against the promise made upstream
Send a real support query and log tone, speed and accuracy of the reply against the voice sheet
Check the unboxing experience against the story told pre-purchase, using recorded footage
Compare the same journey on a top named competitor's site, signal only
Score each step: promise made, promise kept, gap
Repeat quarterly so drift shows over time, not just a one-time snapshot
Route every gap found to the owning specialist (Site, Lifecycle, Ops), not only to brand

name: Run a partnership candidate sourcing sweep
what: Proactively search for non-competitive brands serving the same customer that would make a good collaboration, before any specific proposal exists to screen.
encompasses: Define the target customer overlap criteria from the brand's own avatar record
Search for brands in adjacent categories serving that same customer
Check each candidate is genuinely non-competitive, not just a different product form
Check each candidate's own brand health and reputation before shortlisting
Rank candidates by audience overlap size and narrative fit
Note what each side would plausibly want from the collaboration
Hand the shortlist to the screening step (BRAND-C41) rather than proposing terms itself
Refresh the sweep twice a year so the shortlist does not go stale
outputs: ranked partnership candidate shortlist with fit rationale
founder_sees: Kevin gets a short list of real, non-competitive brands worth reaching out to, before he has to think of any himself.

name: Check reputational risk on a proposed partner, licensee or ambassador

encompasses: Search the candidate's recent public controversies, legal disputes and negative press
Check for statements or associations that conflict with the brand's own claims tiers or values
Check the candidate's own customer or audience sentiment, not just follower count
Check for undisclosed past brand deals that could create a conflict
Flag anything time-sensitive (an active controversy) as a stop, not a caution
Summarize risk as go, go-with-conditions, or no, with the specific evidence
Keep the check to public information only; never private or invented claims
Repeat the check yearly for an ongoing relationship, not just at signing
outputs: risk check summary with evidence and recommendation
trigger: on demand before signing; yearly for ongoing relationships
founder_sees: Kevin sees exactly what a proposed partner has said or done publicly before his name gets attached to theirs.

name: Track a cross-functional initiative end to end (not an idea from the bank)

Fills the gap between single approved ideas the Registrar tracks and full cross-channel launches, for work that spans specialists but is not shaped like a bank idea.
encompasses: open an initiative record with a plain goal, an owner per milestone and a target date
pull status from each specialist's queue without asking them to re-report it elsewhere
flag a milestone at risk before its date, not after
surface blockers that need the founder's decision, not just status
close the initiative with a one-line result and file it for the next similar initiative
distinguish an initiative from a single approved idea so it does not get lost in the registry's per-idea view
outputs: initiative record with milestones and owners
trigger: event: founder opens a multi-specialist initiative
founder_sees: One place to see everything the re-platform, or the new hire, or the new market needs, without chasing five people.

name: Prep the founder before a named external meeting
what: Before a meeting on the founder's calendar with a supplier, investor, agency or platform rep, assemble the relevant numbers, open items and history with that counterparty into a short brief, the way an executive assistant preps a daily brief and meeting notes.
encompasses: match a calendar entry to a known counterparty in the brand brain (vendor, investor, agency)
pull the open items and decisions tied to that counterparty from the registry and decision log
quote the last agreed terms or numbers discussed with them, with dates
flag anything overdue on either side before the meeting
hand the brief to the founder a fixed time before the meeting starts, not after it began
inputs: brand brain: vendor and partner records
trigger: event: a named meeting is coming up on the calendar
founder_sees: A one-pager waiting before the call with the numbers and history already pulled.

name: Draft time-sensitive replies to partners, vendors and press for founder approval
what: When a message arrives from a vendor, a platform, a partner or a journalist that needs a fast answer, draft the reply from the brand brain and the founder's own voice, tiered by risk, and hold it for approval before anything sends. Never sends on its own.
encompasses: detect an incoming message that needs a same-day answer
draft in the founder's voice from stored liked and disliked examples
quote only approved or site-backed facts in the draft, never invent a commitment
tier the draft by risk, a routine confirmation versus anything with a number, a date or a legal word, and gate the risky ones harder
never send; hand the draft to the founder or the named person to send
trigger: event: a message needing a fast reply arrives

external_write.surface: email or messaging platform, draft only, no send

encompasses: pull facts, decisions and action items separately from one transcript
route each action item to the specialist or person who owns it, not to a general inbox
flag a verbal commitment the founder made on the call as a founder-visible follow-up
attach the source transcript timestamp to every extracted item so it can be checked
skip re-logging an item already in the registry from the same conversation

name: Design and maintain the business's own operating cadence

name: Read the funnel net of RTO and COD-versus-prepaid mix, not gross orders

encompasses: split every order-stage number into COD and prepaid before comparing windows
compute a net orders and net revenue figure after expected RTO, alongside the gross figure, never replacing it
flag when the gap between gross and net orders widens 2 or more windows running as its own signal, separate from a demand bottleneck
hold India RTO and COD-share benchmarks, about 25 to 35 percent RTO and 58 to 65 percent COD share as publicly reported, as a comparison band tagged general-practice basis, never this brand's proof

outputs: gross versus net orders and revenue by window

flag a proposed tool that duplicates data the brand already has a source of truth for

mark a proposed tool as needing a migration plan when it would replace a system already holding brand data

pull the plan versus what actually happened, in code where numbers are involved
ask the founder one question: would we do this again the same way

surface the last retro of the same type before the next one of that type starts

flag a pattern of under-delivery against the scope of work running 2 or more periods, not a single bad month

confirm country of origin is stated on product pages that need it

flag a missing disclosure as a blocking failure, not a warning

hold a due-date list separate from the general decisions log

flag a contract with no stored renewal date as incomplete, not silently skip it
diff a renewed contract's terms against the prior version and flag what changed
Log agreed price, MOQ, payment terms and price-lock end date per supplier per SKU
Flag a price lock or contract ending inside a set lead window
Compare the current landed cost against the locked price and flag when the lock is now off-market
Hand a renewal that needs real negotiation to the supplier negotiation process, not auto-renew
outputs: contract and SLA registry with renewal alerts
trigger: event: a new contract is added; continuous for renewal alerts

apply the same structure-and-mood-only rule to adjacent references as to direct competitors

name: Draft a courier or 3PL rate renegotiation using public rate benchmarks

compare the brand's actual paid rate per shipment against the benchmark, by zone and weight slab

flag when a rate contract renewal date is near, so the ask lands before the contract auto-renews

name: Detect audience or metric overlap between two experiments running at once

check a newly approved idea against every currently running entry for audience or window overlap
flag the overlap with which two entries collide and on what dimension
suggest a stagger, a delayed start, rather than blocking the second idea outright
clear the flag automatically once the earlier test's read point passes

outputs: overlap flag with the colliding entries named
trigger: event: a second idea is approved while another is running
founder_sees: A flag before two tests collide, with a suggested stagger.

show a predicted approve, reject or park with the reason pattern it is based on
flag when the ranker's top card and the prediction disagree, before the founder sees either

track prediction accuracy over time and stop showing it if it performs no better than chance
outputs: predicted decision with the reason pattern, attached to the card for internal use
trigger: event: a proposal card is written, before it reaches the founder
founder_sees: Nothing directly; it only changes how a mismatched card is written.

name: Audit what AI shopping agents say about the brand against the claims tiers
what: As merchants now sell through Agentic Storefronts inside ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot, Google AI Mode and Gemini, managed from the Shopify Admin's Knowledge Base app, audit what these AI shopping agents actually say about the brand, price, policy, availability, against the brand's claims tiers, the same way the site and the ad account are audited, since this is now a live customer-facing surface no one else checks.
encompasses: pull or sample what an AI shopping agent states about the brand's products, price and policy
trace each stated claim to an approved or site-backed claim in the brand brain
flag a forbidden or unprovable claim surfaced by an AI agent, the same as a forbidden claim on the site
flag stale price or stock information an AI channel is still repeating after the brand's own data changed
report agent-assisted session performance, engagement, conversion uplift, AOV, next to organic, from the Shopify dashboard's own split
inputs: Shopify Knowledge Base app feed or equivalent
founder_sees: A weekly note on what AI shopping agents are telling customers about the brand, and whether it still matches what is approved.
reassign_reason: What AI shopping agents say about the brand is the same surface as ORG-C37 (AI visibility) and ORG-C36 (correct wrong AI facts). QA keeps the claims-tier check through LOOP-C12. The agent-assisted performance note is a channel read, not a QA pass.

name: Detect a new sales or attribution channel entering the business before it is folded into other
what: As commerce itself changes, an AI shopping agent, a new marketplace, a new payment or messaging partner, catch a new channel entering the business and give it its own named field in the metric contract before its volume gets silently absorbed into other or missed altogether.
encompasses: watch for a new referrer, attribution source or order tag appearing in the data that the current contract has no field for
propose a named field for it, tagged unverified until confirmed with the founder
backfill history for the new channel where the source allows it, and mark earlier periods unavailable where it does not
flag when a growing but unnamed source crosses a materiality threshold, so it cannot be ignored past a certain size
founder_sees: A heads up the first time a new channel shows up in the numbers, before it grows unnoticed.

name: Same-day threshold alert when a metric crosses a hard trigger mid-day
what: Notify before end of day when a metric crosses a hard, pre-agreed trigger mid-day, matching how a head of growth reviews trading dashboards for same-day actions, without waiting for the next daily ranking and without invoking full crisis mode for something short of a crisis.
encompasses: hold a short list of hard triggers with numeric thresholds, agreed in advance, separate from the daily ranking's own thresholds
check live data against the triggers through the day, not only at the daily batch read
notify once per trigger crossing per day, not repeatedly
route the alert to the same-day owner, not necessarily the founder, if one is set
fold the day's crossings into the next daily ranking so nothing is double-counted
founder_sees: A same-day heads up on the one number that crossed a line, instead of finding out tomorrow.
human_role: head of growth; head of ecommerce

name: Reconcile a third-party agency's or platform's reported performance against the metric contract
what: Before the founder trusts an agency's or platform's own performance report, reconcile its numbers against the metric contract's own source-of-truth figures, and flag any vanity-metric framing, a mismatched window, or a number that does not match, since a fractional CMO's reporting rhythm assumes the numbers already agree, and nothing checks that assumption today.
encompasses: match each headline number in the agency's or platform's report to the same field in the metric contract
flag a window mismatch, a different date range used to make a number look better
flag a metric reported that is not in the metric contract's vocabulary at all, and name what it is likely standing in for
recompute period ROAS or a similar ratio in code and compare to the agency's stated figure
state the discrepancy in one line, not just a wall of numbers
trigger: event: an agency or platform report is received
founder_sees: Whether the agency's own report agrees with the brand's own numbers, before it is trusted.

name: Approve, reject or park a proposal card by replying on WhatsApp
what: Let the founder reply to a WhatsApp message with a single word or emoji to approve, reject or park a specific proposal card, matched back to its card id, for when they are mobile-first and away from the review page. Distinct from the traveling-founder voice brief: this is the reply-based decision channel itself.
encompasses: send the card's one-line summary over WhatsApp with a short reply code
match a reply, a word, a number or an emoji, back to the exact card id, even out of order
confirm the decision back in the same thread before it is logged
ask a clarifying question if the reply is ambiguous, rather than guessing
fall back silently to the review page if WhatsApp is not connected for this founder
detect the founder has not opened the review page in the usual window
summarise only the pending decisions, not the full Today screen, into a short spoken-style script
deliver it over the channel the founder already uses, a WhatsApp voice note or a short audio message
accept a reply in the same channel, a word or a voice reply, as the decision, matched back to the card id
fall back to the review page once the founder is active there again
inputs: founder's activity on the review page
outputs: decision logged with reason if given
decision captured from a channel reply
trigger: event: a founder replies to a WhatsApp card message

external_write.surface: WhatsApp Business API, message send and receive only

founder_sees: A card they can approve by typing one word back, from their phone.

merged_from.name: Send the founder a short voice-note style brief for approvals while traveling
merged_from.reason: Both are the founder gate delivered on mobile while away (WhatsApp reply vs voice-note brief). One capability: mobile approvals, with voice or text summary.

name: On-site AI shopping assistant
what: A pre-purchase chat on the site that answers product, size and delivery questions from the catalogue, stock and claims tiers only, and hands off to a person. Different from LIFE-C49 (support actions) and SITE-C73 (third-party agents).
trigger: event: founder approves; weekly transcript and claims review

name: Chargeback and payment dispute responses
what: Build the evidence pack (order, delivery proof, OTP, chat log) for each gateway chargeback or UPI dispute and file it before the deadline. Track win rate by reason code. MONEY-C42 sets alert thresholds but nothing answers disputes.
trigger: event: dispute opened on a payment gateway

name: Courier lost and damaged parcel claims
what: File claims with couriers and aggregators for lost, damaged or wrongly marked RTO shipments, with proof, and track payout against the claim. Only FBA paperwork (PROD-C35) is covered today.
trigger: event: shipment marked lost or damaged, or RTO received damaged; weekly sweep

name: Marketplace reimbursement claims
what: Find and file reimbursements for lost or damaged marketplace inventory and wrong fees (FBA reimbursements, Flipkart SPF, Myntra claims) inside each seller console.

name: Insurance claims
what: Prepare and track claims under transit, stock, cyber and product liability policies, with the evidence each insurer asks for. MONEY-C59 buys cover but nothing files claims.

name: Influencer agreements and ASCI disclosure checks
what: Keep a creator agreement template (deliverables, usage rights, exclusivity, payment, disclosure clause) and check live creator and affiliate posts carry the ASCI and platform disclosure. CREA-C10 tracks rights but no contract or live disclosure check exists.
trigger: event: creator deal agreed; weekly check of live posts

name: Shoot production and model releases
what: Run the shoot: shot list, call sheet, studio or location and model booking, signed model and location releases, retouch QA against the real product, and filing to the asset library. CREA-C12 directs photos; ORG-C06 covers organic batching only.

name: Packaging artwork and mandatory label brief
what: Brief packaging artwork and dielines per channel with mandatory declarations placed (MRP, Legal Metrology, net quantity, BIS or hallmark, EPR mark). PROD-C13 has the spec and LIFE-C25 the unboxing, but no one owns the artwork.
trigger: event: new SKU, new channel or packaging change

name: Festive gifting operations
what: Turn on gift wrap, gift message, price-hidden gift invoice and delivery-by-date cutoffs per pincode for Diwali, Rakhi and wedding season, plus gift guides, and switch them off after the window.
trigger: event: 60 days before each gifting window in LOOP-C05

name: Corporate gifting sales desk
what: Run B2B gifting orders: lead list, quote with bulk tiers, custom packaging or engraving, GST invoice, split delivery to many addresses, and a repeat-order reminder next season. LIFE-C58 has corporate gift card terms only.
trigger: event: inbound corporate enquiry; 90 days before Diwali for outbound

name: Offline retail, stockist and pop-up operations
what: Run the operations of a pop-up, exhibition or stockist: POS setup, stock transfer and return, consignment settlement, staff roster and daily sales reconciliation into the metric contract. BRAND-C42 only designs the event.
trigger: event: pop-up, exhibition or stockist deal approved

name: Subscription payment failure recovery
what: Set retry schedules, card-updater and UPI AutoPay or e-mandate re-authorisation (RBI rules) for failed renewals, and measure involuntary churn apart from cancellations. LIFE-C09 sends the message but no one owns the recovery setup.
trigger: event: failed renewal; monthly involuntary-churn read

name: Mobile app operations (if the brand has an app)
what: App store listing and screenshots, release QA, deep links from ads and email, push opt-in prompt and app-only offers, and app ratings. No record covers an app.
trigger: event: brand has or launches an app; per release

name: Export compliance and international duties
what: Set up IEC and LUT for zero-rated exports, HS codes, commercial invoice and courier export paperwork, and choose DDP vs DDU so the buyer is not surprised by duty. SITE-C12 and PROD-C21 do not cover the paperwork.
trigger: event: first international order or new export market

name: Multi-channel inventory sync and order routing
what: Keep one stock pool across site, marketplaces, quick commerce and stores, with per-channel buffers to stop overselling, and set order routing and split-shipment rules. PROD-C63 only audits mismatches after the fact.

name: GST return preparation and e-way bills
what: Prepare GSTR-1 and 3B, match input credit against GSTR-2B, claim marketplace TCS and TDS credits, and raise e-way bills for B2B and stock transfers. MONEY-C12 tracks thresholds only.
trigger: monthly; event: B2B dispatch or stock transfer

name: Month-end close and management accounts
what: Run a close checklist (bank and gateway recs, accruals, inventory valuation, deferred revenue) and publish management accounts against budget. The pieces exist (MONEY-C51, C53, C56), but nothing owns the close.

name: Product recall and safety incident procedure
what: When a defect is a safety risk, find affected batches, stop sale on every channel, contact buyers, arrange returns or replacements, and log regulator notices. PROD-C73 covers CAPA only, and LOOP-C06 is generic.
trigger: event: safety-related defect or regulator notice

name: Grievance officer queue and consumer notices
what: Run the grievance queue required by India's E-Commerce Rules: acknowledge in 48 hours and resolve in 1 month. Track consumer-forum (e-Daakhil) and legal notices to closure. LOOP-C27 checks the disclosure but nobody works the queue.
trigger: event: grievance or notice received; weekly SLA check

name: Warranty, repair and after-sales service
what: Run resizing, repair, re-plating, warranty and buyback or exchange requests. That means intake, courier pickup, repair partner, status updates and cost per case. This matters for jewellery and durable goods, and returns (LIFE-C26) do not cover it.

name: Made-to-order and personalised order workflow
what: Handle engraving, custom size or made-to-order items: capture the spec at checkout, get the customer's approval on a proof, track production, and state non-returnable terms. No record covers custom orders.
trigger: event: personalised or made-to-order SKU sold
